declarations.statement:
lemma on_param_cos_θ₁₂_eq_zero {V : CKMMatrix} (δ₁₃ : ℝ) (h : Real.cos (θ₁₂ ⟦V⟧) = 0) :

declarations.statement:
lemma on_param_cos_θ₂₃_eq_zero {V : CKMMatrix} (δ₁₃ : ℝ) (h : Real.cos (θ₂₃ ⟦V⟧) = 0) :
    standParam (θ₁₂ ⟦V⟧) (θ₁₃ ⟦V⟧) (θ₂₃ ⟦V⟧) δ₁₃ ≈ standParam (θ₁₂ ⟦V⟧) (θ₁₃ ⟦V⟧) (θ₂₃ ⟦V⟧) 0

declarations.name: standParam.on_param_sin_θ₁₃_eq_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma on_param_sin_θ₁₃_eq_zero {V : CKMMatrix} (δ₁₃ : ℝ) (h : Real.sin (θ₁₃ ⟦V⟧) = 0) :
    standParam (θ₁₂ ⟦V⟧) (θ₁₃ ⟦V⟧) (θ₂₃ ⟦V⟧) δ₁₃ ≈ standParam (θ₁₂ ⟦V⟧) (θ₁₃ ⟦V⟧) (θ₂₃ ⟦V⟧) 0

declarations.name: standParam.on_param_sin_θ₁₂_eq_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma on_param_sin_θ₁₂_eq_zero {V : CKMMatrix} (δ₁₃ : ℝ) (h : Real.sin (θ₁₂ ⟦V⟧) = 0) :
    standParam (θ₁₂ ⟦V⟧) (θ₁₃ ⟦V⟧) (θ₂₃ ⟦V⟧) δ₁₃ ≈ standParam (θ₁₂ ⟦V⟧) (θ₁₃ ⟦V⟧) (θ₂₃ ⟦V⟧) 0

declarations.name: standParam.on_param_sin_θ₂₃_eq_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma on_param_sin_θ₂₃_eq_zero {V : CKMMatrix} (δ₁₃ : ℝ) (h : Real.sin (θ₂₃ ⟦V⟧) = 0) :
    standParam (θ₁₂ ⟦V⟧) (θ₁₃ ⟦V⟧) (θ₂₃ ⟦V⟧) δ₁₃ ≈ standParam (θ₁₂ ⟦V⟧) (θ₁₃ ⟦V⟧) (θ₂₃ ⟦V⟧) 0

declarations.name: standParam.eq_standParam_of_fstRowThdColRealCond
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_standParam_of_fstRowThdColRealCond {V : CKMMatrix} (hb : [V]ud ≠ 0 ∨ [V]us ≠ 0)
    (hV : FstRowThdColRealCond V) : V = standParam (θ₁₂ ⟦V⟧) (θ₁₃ ⟦V⟧) (θ₂₃ ⟦V⟧) (- arg [V]ub)

declarations.statement:
lemma eq_standParam_of_ubOnePhaseCond {V : CKMMatrix} (hV : ubOnePhaseCond V) :
    V = standParam (θ₁₂ ⟦V⟧) (θ₁₃ ⟦V⟧) (θ₂₃ ⟦V⟧) 0

declarations.name: standParam.exists_δ₁₃
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_δ₁₃ (V : CKMMatrix) :
    ∃ (δ₃ : ℝ), V ≈ standParam (θ₁₂ ⟦V⟧) (θ₁₃ ⟦V⟧) (θ₂₃ ⟦V⟧) δ₃

declarations.name: standParam.eq_standardParameterization_δ₃
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_standardParameterization_δ₃ (V : CKMMatrix) :
    V ≈ standParam (θ₁₂ ⟦V⟧) (θ₁₃ ⟦V⟧) (θ₂₃ ⟦V⟧) (δ₁₃ ⟦V⟧)

declarations.name: standParam.exists_for_CKMatrix
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_for_CKMatrix (V : CKMMatrix) :
    ∃ (θ₁₂ θ₁₃ θ₂₃ δ₁₃ : ℝ), V ≈ standParam θ₁₂ θ₁₃ θ₂₃ δ₁₃

modules.title: The PMNS matrix
modules.doc: The definition the PMNS matrix, which describes neutrino oscillations as part of U(3).

declarations.name: diagPhase
declarations.doc: diagonal phase matrix from a real-valued function on indices
declarations.statement: def diagPhase (θ : Fin 3 → ℝ) : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ

declarations.name: diagPhase_zero
declarations.doc: lemma stating that the diagonal phase matrix with all zeros is the identity matrix
declarations.statement:
lemma diagPhase_zero:
    diagPhase (fun _ : Fin 3 => 0) = 1

declarations.name: diagPhase_zero_eq
declarations.doc: lemma stating that diagPhase with θ = 0 is equal to diagPhase with all zero phases
declarations.statement: lemma diagPhase_zero_eq : diagPhase 0 = diagPhase (fun _ : Fin 3 => 0)

declarations.name: diagPhase_star
declarations.doc:
lemma stating that the Hermitian conjugate of diagPhase diag(+iθ_i)
is just diagPhase with entries diag(-iθ_i)
declarations.statement:
lemma diagPhase_star (θ : Fin 3 → ℝ) :
    (diagPhase θ)ᴴ = diagPhase (- θ)

declarations.name: diagPhase_mul
declarations.doc: lemma stating that multiplying two phase matrices is equivalent to adding the phases
declarations.statement:
lemma diagPhase_mul (θ φ : Fin 3 → ℝ) :
    diagPhase θ * diagPhase φ = diagPhase (θ + φ)

declarations.name: diagPhaseUnitary
declarations.doc: diagonal phase matrix diag(iθ_i) is part of the unitary group
declarations.statement: def diagPhaseUnitary (θ : Fin 3 → ℝ) : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ

declarations.name: diagPhaseShift_coe_matrix
declarations.doc:
The underlying matrix of the phase-shift element of the unitary group is the
phase-shift matrix.
declarations.statement: lemma diagPhaseShift_coe_matrix (θ : Fin 3 → ℝ) : ↑(diagPhaseUnitary θ) = diagPhase θ

declarations.name: leptonPhaseShift
declarations.doc:
The Lepton phase shift matrix as a `3×3` complex matrix, given three reals `a b c`.
This dictates the phase shift freedom of the charged lepton sector.
declarations.statement: def leptonPhaseShift (a b c : ℝ) : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ

declarations.name: neutrinoPhaseShift
declarations.doc:
The neutrino phase shift matrix as a `3×3` complex matrix, given three reals `d e f`.
This dictates the phase shift freedom of the neutrino sector (If neutrinos are Dirac).
declarations.statement: def neutrinoPhaseShift (d e f : ℝ) : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ

declarations.name: majoranaPhaseMatrix
declarations.doc:
If neutrinos are Majorana particles, then the neutrino phase shift matrix is physical,
and cannot be absorbed into the definition of the neutrino fields.
declarations.statement: def majoranaPhaseMatrix (α1 α2 : ℝ) : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ

declarations.name: PMNSDiracEquivalence
declarations.doc: The Dirac PMNS matrix equivalence relations
declarations.statement: def PMNSDiracEquivalence (U V : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) : Prop

declarations.name: PMNSDiracEquivalence_refl
declarations.doc: The relation `PMNSDiracEquivalence` is reflexive.
declarations.statement:
lemma PMNSDiracEquivalence_refl :
    ∀ U : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ, PMNSDiracEquivalence U U

declarations.name: PMNSDiracEquivalence_symm
declarations.doc: The relation `PMNSDiracEquivalence` is symmetric.
declarations.statement:
lemma PMNSDiracEquivalence_symm :
    ∀ U V : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ, PMNSDiracEquivalence U V → PMNSDiracEquivalence V U

declarations.name: PMNSDiracEquivalence_trans
declarations.doc: The relation `PMNSDiracEquivalence` is transitive.
declarations.statement:
lemma PMNSDiracEquivalence_trans {U V W : unitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ} :
    PMNSDiracEquivalence U V → PMNSDiracEquivalence V W → PMNSDiracEquivalence U W

modules.title: Anomaly cancellation conditions for the n-family SM.
modules.doc: We define the ACC system for the Standard Model with`n`-families and no RHN.

declarations.name: SMCharges
declarations.doc: Associate to each (including RHN) SM fermion a set of charges
declarations.statement: def SMCharges (n : ℕ) : ACCSystemCharges

declarations.name: SMSpecies
declarations.doc: The vector space associated with a single species of fermions.
declarations.statement: def SMSpecies (n : ℕ) : ACCSystemCharges

declarations.name: SMCharges.sum_SMSpecies_numberCharges_one
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_SMSpecies_numberCharges_one {M} [AddCommMonoid M]
    (f : Fin (SMSpecies 1).numberCharges → M) :
    ∑ i, f i = f ⟨0, by simp⟩

declarations.name: SMCharges.toSpeciesEquiv
declarations.doc:
An equivalence between the set `(SMCharges n).charges` and the set
`(Fin 5 → Fin n → ℚ)`.
declarations.statement: def toSpeciesEquiv : (SMCharges n).Charges ≃ (Fin 5 → Fin (SMSpecies n).numberCharges → ℚ)

declarations.name: SMCharges.toSpecies
declarations.doc: For a given `i ∈ Fin 5`, the projection of a charge onto that species.
declarations.statement: def toSpecies (i : Fin 5) : (SMCharges n).Charges →ₗ[ℚ] (SMSpecies n).Charges

declarations.name: SMCharges.toSpecies_apply_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma toSpecies_apply_eq (i : Fin 5) (S : (SMCharges n).Charges) :
    toSpecies i S = fun j => toSpeciesEquiv S i j

declarations.name: SMCharges.charges_eq_toSpecies_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma charges_eq_toSpecies_eq (S T : (SMCharges n).Charges) :
    S = T ↔ ∀ i, toSpecies i S = toSpecies i T

declarations.name: SMCharges.toSMSpecies_toSpecies_inv
declarations.statement:
lemma toSMSpecies_toSpecies_inv (i : Fin 5) (f : Fin 5 → Fin n → ℚ) :
    (toSpecies i) (toSpeciesEquiv.symm f) = f i

declarations.name: SMCharges.Q

declarations.doc: Extensionality lemma for `accGrav`.

declarations.name: SMACCs.accSU2
declarations.doc: The `SU(2)` anomaly equation.
declarations.statement: def accSU2 : (SMCharges n).Charges →ₗ[ℚ] ℚ

declarations.name: SMACCs.accSU2_ext
declarations.doc: Extensionality lemma for `accSU2`.

declarations.name: SMACCs.accSU3
declarations.doc: The `SU(3)` anomaly equations.
declarations.statement: def accSU3 : (SMCharges n).Charges →ₗ[ℚ] ℚ

declarations.name: SMACCs.accSU3_ext
declarations.doc: Extensionality lemma for `accSU3`.

declarations.name: SMACCs.accYY
declarations.doc: The `Y²` anomaly equation.
declarations.statement: def accYY : (SMCharges n).Charges →ₗ[ℚ] ℚ

declarations.name: SMACCs.accYY_ext
declarations.doc: Extensionality lemma for `accYY`.

declarations.name: SMACCs.quadBiLin
declarations.doc: The quadratic bilinear map.
declarations.statement: def quadBiLin : BiLinearSymm (SMCharges n).Charges

declarations.doc: The quadratic anomaly cancellation condition.
declarations.statement: def accQuad : HomogeneousQuadratic (SMCharges n).Charges

declarations.doc: Extensionality lemma for `accQuad`.

lemma accQuad_ext {S T : (SMCharges n).Charges}
    (h : ∀ j, ∑ i, ((fun a => a^2) ∘ toSpecies j S) i =

The embedding of the `1`-family charges into the `n`-family charges in

modules.title: Anomaly Cancellation in the Standard Model without Gravity
modules.doc:
This file defines the system of anomaly equations for the SM without RHN, and
without the gravitational ACC.

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav
declarations.doc: The ACC system for the standard model without RHN and without the gravitational ACC.
declarations.statement: def SMNoGrav (n : ℕ) : ACCSystem

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.SU2Sol
declarations.doc: The charges in `(SMNoGrav n).LinSols` satisfy the `SU(2)` anomaly-equation.
declarations.statement: lemma SU2Sol (S : (SMNoGrav n).LinSols) : accSU2 S.val = 0

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.SU3Sol
declarations.doc: The charges in `(SMNoGrav n).LinSols` satisfy the `SU(3)` anomaly-equation.
declarations.statement: lemma SU3Sol (S : (SMNoGrav n).LinSols) : accSU3 S.val = 0

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.cubeSol
declarations.doc: The charges in `(SMNoGrav n).Sols` satisfy the cubic anomaly-equation.
declarations.statement: lemma cubeSol (S : (SMNoGrav n).Sols) : accCube S.val = 0

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.chargeToLinear
declarations.doc:
An element of `charges` which satisfies the linear ACCs
gives us a element of `AnomalyFreeLinear`.
declarations.statement:
def chargeToLinear (S : (SMNoGrav n).Charges) (hSU2 : accSU2 S = 0) (hSU3 : accSU3 S = 0) :
    (SMNoGrav n).LinSols

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.linearToQuad
declarations.doc:
An element of `AnomalyFreeLinear` which satisfies the quadratic ACCs
gives us a element of `AnomalyFreeQuad`.
declarations.statement: def linearToQuad (S : (SMNoGrav n).LinSols) : (SMNoGrav n).QuadSols

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.quadToAF
declarations.doc:
An element of `AnomalyFreeQuad` which satisfies the quadratic ACCs
gives us a element of `AnomalyFree`.
declarations.statement:
def quadToAF (S : (SMNoGrav n).QuadSols) (hc : accCube S.val = 0) :
    (SMNoGrav n).Sols

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.chargeToQuad
declarations.doc:
An element of `charges` which satisfies the linear and quadratic ACCs
gives us a element of `AnomalyFreeQuad`.
declarations.statement:
def chargeToQuad (S : (SMNoGrav n).Charges) (hSU2 : accSU2 S = 0) (hSU3 : accSU3 S = 0) :
    (SMNoGrav n).QuadSols

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.chargeToAF
declarations.doc:
An element of `charges` which satisfies the linear, quadratic and cubic ACCs
gives us a element of `AnomalyFree`.
declarations.statement:
def chargeToAF (S : (SMNoGrav n).Charges) (hSU2 : accSU2 S = 0) (hSU3 : accSU3 S = 0)
    (hc : accCube S = 0) : (SMNoGrav n).Sols

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.linearToAF
declarations.doc:
An element of `AnomalyFreeLinear` which satisfies the quadratic and cubic ACCs
gives us a element of `AnomalyFree`.
declarations.statement:
def linearToAF (S : (SMNoGrav n).LinSols)
    (hc : accCube S.val = 0) : (SMNoGrav n).Sols

modules.title: Lemmas for 1 family SM Accs
modules.doc:
The main result of this file is the conclusion of this paper:
  [Lohitsiri and Tong][Lohitsiri:2019fuu] [ref: Lohitsiri:2019fuu]

That every solution to the ACCs without gravity satisfies for free the gravitational anomaly.

## References

* The main result of this file is the conclusion of this paper. [ref: Lohitsiri:2019fuu]

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.E_zero_iff_Q_zero
declarations.doc:
For a set of 1 family SM charges satisfying all ACCs except the gravitational,
the charge of `Q` is zero if and only if `E` is zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma E_zero_iff_Q_zero {S : (SMNoGrav 1).Sols} : Q S.val (0 : Fin 1) = 0 ↔
    E S.val (0 : Fin 1) = 0

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.accGrav_Q_zero
declarations.doc:
For a set of 1-family SM charges satisfying all ACCs except the gravitational,
if the `Q` charge is zero then the charges satisfy the gravitational ACCs.
declarations.statement:
lemma accGrav_Q_zero {S : (SMNoGrav 1).Sols} (hQ : Q S.val (0 : Fin 1) = 0) :
    accGrav S.val = 0

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.accGrav_Q_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
For a set of 1-family SM charges satisfying all ACCs except the gravitational,
if the `Q` charge is not zero then the charges satisfy the gravitational ACCs.
declarations.statement:
lemma accGrav_Q_ne_zero {S : (SMNoGrav 1).Sols} (hQ : Q S.val (0 : Fin 1) ≠ 0) :
    accGrav S.val = 0

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.accGravSatisfied
declarations.doc: Any solution to the 1-family ACCs without gravity satisfies the gravitational ACC.
declarations.statement:
theorem accGravSatisfied {S : (SMNoGrav 1).Sols} :
    accGrav S.val = 0

modules.title: Parameterizations for solutions to the linear ACCs for 1 family
modules.doc:
In this file we give two parameterizations
- `linearParameters` of solutions to the linear ACCs for 1 family
- `linearParametersQENeqZero` of solutions to the linear ACCs for 1 family with Q and E non-zero

## References

* These parameterizations are based on https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.00514.
  [ref: Lohitsiri:2019fuu]

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.linearParameters
declarations.doc: The parameters for a linear parameterization to the solution of the linear ACCs.
declarations.statement:
structure linearParameters where
  /-- The parameter `Q'`. -/
  Q' : ℚ
  /-- The parameter `Y`. -/
  Y : ℚ
  /-- The parameter `E'`. -/
  E' : ℚ

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.linearParameters.ext
declarations.statement:
lemma ext {S T : linearParameters} (hQ : S.Q' = T.Q') (hY : S.Y = T.Y) (hE : S.E' = T.E') :
    S = T

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.linearParameters.asCharges
declarations.doc: The map from the linear parameters to elements of `(SMNoGrav 1).charges`.
declarations.statement: def asCharges (S : linearParameters) : (SMNoGrav 1).Charges

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.linearParameters.speciesVal
declarations.statement:
lemma speciesVal (S : linearParameters) :
    toSpeciesEquiv S.asCharges= fun i _ => S.asCharges i

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.linearParameters.toSpecies_apply_asCharges
declarations.statement:
lemma toSpecies_apply_asCharges (S : linearParameters) (i : Fin 5) :
    toSpecies i S.asCharges = fun _ => S.asCharges i

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.linearParameters.asLinear
declarations.doc: The map from the linear parameters to elements of `(SMNoGrav 1).LinSols`.
declarations.statement: def asLinear (S : linearParameters) : (SMNoGrav 1).LinSols

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.linearParameters.asLinear_val
declarations.statement: lemma asLinear_val (S : linearParameters) : S.asLinear.val = S.asCharges

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.linearParameters.cubic
declarations.statement:
lemma cubic (S : linearParameters) :
    accCube (S.asCharges) = - 54 * S.Q'^3 - 18 * S.Q' * S.Y ^ 2 + S.E'^3

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.linearParameters.cubic_zero_Q'_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma cubic_zero_Q'_zero (S : linearParameters) (hc : accCube (S.asCharges) = 0)
    (h : S.Q' = 0) : S.E' = 0

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.linearParameters.cubic_zero_E'_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma cubic_zero_E'_zero (S : linearParameters) (hc : accCube (S.asCharges) = 0)
    (h : S.E' = 0) : S.Q' = 0

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.linearParameters.bijection
declarations.doc: The bijection between the type of linear parameters and `(SMNoGrav 1).LinSols`.
declarations.statement: def bijection : linearParameters ≃ (SMNoGrav 1).LinSols

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.linearParameters.bijectionQEZero
declarations.doc:
The bijection between the linear parameters and `(SMNoGrav 1).LinSols` in the special
case when Q and E are both not zero.
declarations.statement:
def bijectionQEZero : {S : linearParameters // S.Q' ≠ 0 ∧ S.E' ≠ 0} ≃
    {S : (SMNoGrav 1).LinSols // Q S.val (0 : Fin 1) ≠ 0 ∧ E S.val (0 : Fin 1) ≠ 0}

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.linearParameters.grav
declarations.statement:
lemma grav (S : linearParameters) :
    accGrav S.asCharges = 0 ↔ S.E' = 6 * S.Q'

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.linearParametersQENeqZero
declarations.doc:
The parameters for solutions to the linear ACCs with the condition that Q and E are
non-zero.
declarations.statement:
structure linearParametersQENeqZero where
  /-- The parameter `x`. -/
  x : ℚ
  /-- The parameter `v`. -/
  v : ℚ
  /-- The parameter `w`. -/
  w : ℚ
  hx : x ≠ 0
  hvw : v + w ≠ 0

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.linearParametersQENeqZero.ext
declarations.statement:
lemma ext {S T : linearParametersQENeqZero} (hx : S.x = T.x) (hv : S.v = T.v)
    (hw : S.w = T.w) : S = T

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.linearParametersQENeqZero.toLinearParameters
declarations.doc: A map from `linearParametersQENeqZero` to `linearParameters`.
declarations.statement:
def toLinearParameters (S : linearParametersQENeqZero) :
    {S : linearParameters // S.Q' ≠ 0 ∧ S.E' ≠ 0}

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.linearParametersQENeqZero.tolinearParametersQNeqZero
declarations.doc:
A map from `linearParameters` to `linearParametersQENeqZero` in the special case when
`Q'` and `E'` of the linear parameters are non-zero.
declarations.statement:
def tolinearParametersQNeqZero (S : {S : linearParameters // S.Q' ≠ 0 ∧ S.E' ≠ 0}) :
    linearParametersQENeqZero

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.linearParametersQENeqZero.bijectionLinearParameters
declarations.doc:
A bijection between the type `linearParametersQENeqZero` and linear parameters
with `Q'` and `E'` non-zero.
declarations.statement:
def bijectionLinearParameters :
    linearParametersQENeqZero ≃ {S : linearParameters // S.Q' ≠ 0 ∧ S.E' ≠ 0}

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.linearParametersQENeqZero.bijection
declarations.doc: The bijection between `linearParametersQENeqZero` and `LinSols` with `Q` and `E` non-zero.
declarations.statement:
def bijection : linearParametersQENeqZero ≃
    {S : (SMNoGrav 1).LinSols // Q S.val (0 : Fin 1) ≠ 0 ∧ E S.val (0 : Fin 1) ≠ 0}

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.linearParametersQENeqZero.bijection_coe_val
declarations.statement:
lemma bijection_coe_val (S : linearParametersQENeqZero) :
    (bijection S).1.val = (bijectionLinearParameters S : linearParameters).asCharges

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.linearParametersQENeqZero.cubic
declarations.statement:
lemma cubic (S : linearParametersQENeqZero) :
    accCube (bijection S).1.val = 0 ↔ S.v ^ 3 + S.w ^ 3 = -1

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.linearParametersQENeqZero.cubic_v_or_w_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma cubic_v_or_w_zero (S : linearParametersQENeqZero) (h : accCube (bijection S).1.val = 0) :
    S.v = 0 ∨ S.w = 0

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.linearParametersQENeqZero.cubic_v_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma cubic_v_zero (S : linearParametersQENeqZero) (h : accCube (bijection S).1.val = 0)
    (hv : S.v = 0) : S.w = -1

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.linearParametersQENeqZero.cube_w_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma cube_w_zero (S : linearParametersQENeqZero) (h : accCube (bijection S).1.val = 0)
    (hw : S.w = 0) : S.v = -1

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.linearParametersQENeqZero.cube_w_v
declarations.statement:
lemma cube_w_v (S : linearParametersQENeqZero) (h : accCube (bijection S).1.val = 0) :
    (S.v = -1 ∧ S.w = 0) ∨ (S.v = 0 ∧ S.w = -1)

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.linearParametersQENeqZero.grav
declarations.statement: lemma grav (S : linearParametersQENeqZero) : accGrav (bijection S).1.val = 0 ↔ S.v + S.w = -1

declarations.name: SM.SMNoGrav.One.linearParametersQENeqZero.grav_of_cubic
declarations.statement:
lemma grav_of_cubic (S : linearParametersQENeqZero) (h : accCube (bijection S).1.val = 0) :
    accGrav (bijection S).1.val = 0

modules.title: Permutations of SM with no RHN.
modules.doc: We define the group of permutations for the SM charges with no RHN.

declarations.name: SM.PermGroup
declarations.doc: The group of `Sₙ` permutations for each species.
declarations.statement: def PermGroup (n : ℕ)

declarations.doc:
The type `PermGroup n` inherits the instance of a group from it's
target space `Equiv.Perm`.
declarations.statement: instance : Group (PermGroup n)

declarations.name: SM.chargeMap
declarations.doc: The image of an element of `permGroup n` under the representation on charges.
declarations.statement: def chargeMap (f : PermGroup n) : (SMCharges n).Charges →ₗ[ℚ] (SMCharges n).Charges

declarations.name: SM.repCharges
declarations.doc: The representation of `(permGroup n)` acting on the vector space of charges.
declarations.statement: def repCharges {n : ℕ} : Representation ℚ (PermGroup n) (SMCharges n).Charges

declarations.name: SM.repCharges_toSpecies
declarations.doc:
The species charges of a set of charges acted on by a family permutation is the permutation
of those species charges with the corresponding part of the family permutation.
declarations.statement:
lemma repCharges_toSpecies (f : PermGroup n) (S : (SMCharges n).Charges) (j : Fin 5) :
    toSpecies j (repCharges f S) = toSpecies j S ∘ f⁻¹ j

declarations.name: SM.toSpecies_sum_invariant
declarations.doc:
The sum over every charge in any species to some power `m` is invariant under the group
action.
declarations.statement:
lemma toSpecies_sum_invariant (m : ℕ) (f : PermGroup n) (S : (SMCharges n).Charges) (j : Fin 5) :
    ∑ i, ((fun a => a ^ m) ∘ toSpecies j (repCharges f S)) i =
    ∑ i, ((fun a => a ^ m) ∘ toSpecies j S) i

declarations.name: SM.accGrav_invariant
declarations.doc: The gravitational anomaly equations is invariant under family permutations.
declarations.statement:
lemma accGrav_invariant (f : PermGroup n) (S : (SMCharges n).Charges) :
    accGrav (repCharges f S) = accGrav S

declarations.name: SM.accSU2_invariant
declarations.doc: The `SU(2)` anomaly equation is invariant under family permutations.
declarations.statement:
lemma accSU2_invariant (f : PermGroup n) (S : (SMCharges n).Charges) :
    accSU2 (repCharges f S) = accSU2 S

declarations.name: SM.accSU3_invariant
declarations.doc: The `SU(3)` anomaly equation is invariant under family permutations.
declarations.statement:
lemma accSU3_invariant (f : PermGroup n) (S : (SMCharges n).Charges) :
    accSU3 (repCharges f S) = accSU3 S

declarations.name: SM.accYY_invariant
declarations.doc: The `Y²` anomaly equation is invariant under family permutations.
declarations.statement:

modules.title: Down-type singlets
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The Standard Model down-type singlet is a right-handed Weyl spinor in the `(3, 1)_{-2}`
representation. Here charges are normalized as `6Y`, so `-2` is the usual hypercharge
`Y = -1/3`.

`DownSinglet` is the target vector space of one down-type quark multiplet. Its Weyl factor
carries the Lorentz index and its three-dimensional factor carries the colour index. The absence
of a weak factor makes it an `SU(2)` singlet.

The Lorentz and gauge actions are first defined separately. The gauge action is then computed on a
basis, used to identify its kernel, and descended to each supported global form of the Standard
Model gauge group.

## ii. Key results

- `DownSinglet` : the target space of the `(3, 1)_{-2}` multiplet.
- `repLorentzGroup` : the right-handed Lorentz action.
- `repGaugeGroupI` : the action of the unquotiented gauge group.
- `repGaugeGroupI_tmul_basis_eq_sum` : the gauge action in a tensor-product basis.
- `mem_repGaugeGroupI_ker_iff_eq` : the kernel of the full-group action.
- `gaugeGroup_subgroup_ℤ₆_le_ker_repGaugeGroupI` : triviality of the central `ℤ₆`.
- `repGaugeGroup` : the action descended to every supported gauge-group quotient.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The down-singlet space
- B. Linear structure
- C. Lorentz action
- D. Gauge action
- E. Kernel of the gauge action
- F. Descent to quotient gauge groups

sections.text:
## A. The down-singlet space

The Weyl factor carries the right-handed Lorentz index, while
`EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 3)` carries the colour index.

## B. Linear structure

`DownSinglet` wraps its tensor-product carrier as a distinct type. The equivalences below identify
the two types and transport the additive and complex module structures to `DownSinglet`.

## C. Lorentz action

The Lorentz group acts on the right-handed Weyl factor and leaves the colour index fixed.

## D. Gauge action

The `SU(3)` component acts on the colour index, while the `SU(2)` component acts trivially. The
`U(1)` action is `star z ^ 2`; since `z` is unitary, `star z = z⁻¹`, so this represents charge
`-2`.

The tensor and basis formulas below expose the coefficients used to compare actions and compute the
kernel.

## E. Kernel of the gauge action

An element acts trivially when its colour action is scalar and that scalar cancels its `U(1)`
phase. Its weak component is unrestricted because the down-type singlet is an `SU(2)` singlet.

## F. Descent to quotient gauge groups

A representation descends through a quotient when the quotient subgroup lies in its kernel. For
the central `ℤ₆`, the colour phase is `x²` while the charge `-2` phase is `(star x)² = x⁻²`, so
their product is one.

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet
declarations.doc:
The target vector space of one Standard Model down-type singlet quark.
It carries the `(3, 1)_{-2}` representation of the gauge group.
declarations.statement:
structure DownSinglet where
  /-- The right-handed Weyl spinor with its colour index. -/
  val : Fermion.RightHandedWeyl ⊗[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 3)

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.valEquiv
declarations.doc: Identifies a down-type singlet with its underlying tensor-product value.
declarations.statement: def valEquiv : DownSinglet ≃ Fermion.RightHandedWeyl ⊗[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 3)
instance : AddCommGroup DownSinglet
instance : Module ℂ DownSinglet

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.valLinEquiv
declarations.doc: The linear identification with the underlying tensor product.
declarations.statement:
def valLinEquiv : DownSinglet ≃ₗ[ℂ]

declarations.statement: lemma valLinEquiv_apply (d : DownSinglet) : valLinEquiv d = d.val

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.valLinEquiv_symm_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma valLinEquiv_symm_apply
    (m : Fermion.RightHandedWeyl ⊗[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 3)) :
    valLinEquiv.symm m = ⟨m⟩

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.val_add
declarations.statement: lemma val_add (d₁ d₂ : DownSinglet) : (d₁ + d₂).val = d₁.val + d₂.val

declarations.statement: lemma val_smul (r : ℂ) (d : DownSinglet) : (r • d).val = r • d.val

declarations.doc: The right-handed Lorentz representation on down-type singlet quarks.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def repLorentzGroup : Representation ℂ (SL(2,ℂ)) DownSinglet

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.repGaugeGroupI
declarations.doc: The `(3, 1)_{-2}` action of the unquotiented Standard Model gauge group.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def repGaugeGroupI : Representation ℂ GaugeGroupI DownSinglet

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.repGaugeGroupI_tmul
declarations.doc: The gauge action on a pure spinor–colour tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_tmul (g : GaugeGroupI) (ψ : Fermion.RightHandedWeyl)
    (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 3)) :
    repGaugeGroupI g ⟨ψ ⊗ₜ v⟩ =
      ⟨(star g.toU1.1 ^ 2) • ψ ⊗ₜ g.toSU3.1.toEuclideanLin v⟩

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.repGaugeGroupI_tmul_basis_eq_sum
declarations.doc: Expands the gauge action in the spinor–colour basis.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_tmul_basis_eq_sum (g : GaugeGroupI) (k : Fin 2) (i : Fin 3) :
    repGaugeGroupI g
      ⟨RightHandedWeyl.basis k ⊗ₜ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin 3) ℂ i⟩ =
      ∑ i' : Fin 3, (star g.toU1.1 ^ 2 * g.toSU3.1 i' i) •
        (⟨RightHandedWeyl.basis k ⊗ₜ[ℂ]
          EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin 3) ℂ i'⟩ : DownSinglet)

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.repGaugeGroupI_eq_iff_mul_eq
declarations.doc:
Two gauge elements induce the same action exactly when their hypercharge–colour coefficients
agree.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_eq_iff_mul_eq {g₁ g₂ : GaugeGroupI} :
    repGaugeGroupI g₁ = repGaugeGroupI g₂ ↔ ∀ i i',
      star g₁.toU1.1 ^ 2 * g₁.toSU3.1 i' i =
        star g₂.toU1.1 ^ 2 * g₂.toSU3.1 i' i

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.mem_repGaugeGroupI_ker_iff_eq
declarations.doc: Characterizes the full-group elements acting trivially on the down-type singlet.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_repGaugeGroupI_ker_iff_eq {g : GaugeGroupI} :
    g ∈ repGaugeGroupI.ker ↔ ∃ a : ℂ,
      g.toSU3.1 = a • 1 ∧ a * star g.toU1.1 ^ 2 = 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.gaugeGroup_subgroup_ℤ₆_le_ker_repGaugeGroupI
declarations.doc: The central `ℤ₆` subgroup acts trivially on `(3, 1)_{-2}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeGroup_subgroup_ℤ₆_le_ker_repGaugeGroupI :
    GaugeGroupQuot.subgroup .ℤ₆ ≤ repGaugeGroupI.ker

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.gaugeGroup_subgroup_le_ker_repGaugeGroupI
declarations.doc: Every supported quotient subgroup acts trivially on the down-type singlet.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeGroup_subgroup_le_ker_repGaugeGroupI (Q : GaugeGroupQuot) :
    Q.subgroup ≤ repGaugeGroupI.ker

declarations.name: StandardModel.DownSinglet.repGaugeGroup
declarations.doc:
The `(3, 1)_{-2}` representation for every supported global form of the
Standard Model gauge group.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def repGaugeGroup : (Q : GaugeGroupQuot) →
    Representation ℂ (GaugeGroup Q) DownSinglet

modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The Standard Model lepton doublet is a left-handed Weyl spinor in the `(1, 2)_{-3}`
representation. Here charges are normalized as `6Y`, so `-3` is the usual hypercharge
`Y = -1/2`.

`LeptonDoublet` is the target vector space of one lepton multiplet. Its Weyl factor
carries the Lorentz index and its two-dimensional factor carries the weak index.
The absence of a colour factor makes it an `SU(3)` singlet.

The Lorentz and gauge actions are first defined separately. The gauge action is then
computed on a basis, used to identify its kernel, and descended to each supported global
form of the Standard Model gauge group.

## ii. Key results

- `LeptonDoublet` : the target space of the `(1, 2)_{-3}` multiplet.
- `repLorentzGroup` : the left-handed Lorentz action.
- `repGaugeGroupI` : the action of the unquotiented gauge group.
- `repGaugeGroupI_tmul_basis_eq_sum` : the gauge action in a tensor-product basis.
- `mem_repGaugeGroupI_ker_iff_eq` : the kernel of the full-group action.
- `gaugeGroup_subgroup_ℤ₆_le_ker_repGaugeGroupI` : triviality of the central `ℤ₆`.

## iii. Table of contents

- B. Linear structure
- C. Lorentz action
- D. Gauge action
- E. Kernel of the gauge action
- F. Descent to quotient gauge groups

sections.text:
## A. The lepton-doublet space

The Weyl factor carries the left-handed Lorentz index, while
`EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 2)` carries the weak index.

## B. Linear structure

The wrapper distinguishes lepton doublets from other isomorphic vector spaces.
The following equivalences transfer the linear structure of the tensor product and expose
that model when defining representations.

## C. Lorentz action

The Lorentz group acts on the left-handed Weyl factor and leaves the weak index fixed.

## D. Gauge action

The colour factor acts trivially, while `SU(2)` acts on the weak index. The `U(1)` action
is `star z ^ 3`; since `z` is unitary, `star z = z⁻¹`, so this represents charge `-3`.

The tensor and basis formulas below expose the coefficients used to compare actions and
compute the kernel.

## E. Kernel of the gauge action

An element acts trivially when its weak action is scalar and that scalar cancels its
`U(1)` phase. Its colour component is unrestricted because the lepton doublet is an
`SU(3)` singlet.

## F. Descent to quotient gauge groups

A representation descends through a quotient when the quotient subgroup lies in its
kernel. For the central `ℤ₆`, the weak central phase and charge `-3` phase combine to a
sixth power and therefore act trivially.

modules.title: Charged-lepton singlets
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The Standard Model charged-lepton singlet is a right-handed Weyl spinor in the `(1, 1)_{-6}`
representation. Here charges are normalized as `6Y`, so `-6` is the usual hypercharge
`Y = -1`.

`LeptonSinglet` is the target vector space of one charged-lepton singlet. Its only index is
the Lorentz index carried by the Weyl spinor.

The Lorentz and gauge actions are first defined separately. The gauge action is then computed
on an arbitrary spinor, used to identify its kernel, and descended to each supported global
form of the Standard Model gauge group.

## ii. Key results

- `LeptonSinglet` : the target space of the `(1, 1)_{-6}` multiplet.
- `repLorentzGroup` : the right-handed Lorentz action.
- `repGaugeGroupI` : the action of the unquotiented gauge group.
- `repGaugeGroupI_apply` : the gauge action on a spinor.
- `mem_repGaugeGroupI_ker_iff_eq` : the kernel of the full-group action.
- `gaugeGroup_subgroup_ℤ₆_le_ker_repGaugeGroupI` : triviality of the central `ℤ₆`.
- `repGaugeGroup` : the action descended to every supported gauge-group quotient.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The charged-lepton-singlet space
- B. Linear structure
- C. Lorentz action
- D. Gauge action
- E. Kernel of the gauge action
- F. Descent to quotient gauge groups

sections.text:
## A. The charged-lepton-singlet space

The Weyl spinor carries the right-handed Lorentz index, and it is the whole of the multiplet:
a charged-lepton singlet has no colour index and no weak-isospin index.

## B. Linear structure

The wrapper distinguishes charged-lepton singlets from other isomorphic vector spaces.
The following equivalences transfer the linear structure of the Weyl-spinor space and expose
that model when defining representations.

## C. Lorentz action

The Lorentz group acts through the right-handed Weyl representation, transported along the
identification of a charged-lepton singlet with its spinor.

## D. Gauge action

The colour and weak factors act trivially, so the gauge group acts only through hypercharge.
The `U(1)` action is `star z ^ 6`; since `z` is unitary, `star z = z⁻¹`, so this represents
charge `-6`.

The formulas below expose the scalar used to compare actions and compute the kernel.

## E. Kernel of the gauge action

An element acts trivially exactly when its hypercharge scalar is one. Its colour and weak
components are unrestricted, since neither appears in the action.

## F. Descent to quotient gauge groups

A representation descends through a quotient when the quotient subgroup lies in its kernel.
The `U(1)` component of a central element is a sixth root of unity, so conjugating and raising
to the sixth power gives one, and charge `-6` therefore acts trivially.

def valLinEquiv : QuarkDoublet ≃ₗ[ℂ]
    Fermion.LeftHandedWeyl ⊗[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 3) ⊗[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 2)

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.valLinEquiv_apply
declarations.statement: lemma valLinEquiv_apply (q : QuarkDoublet) : valLinEquiv q = q.val

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.valLinEquiv_symm_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma valLinEquiv_symm_apply
    (m : Fermion.LeftHandedWeyl ⊗[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 3) ⊗[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 2)) :
    valLinEquiv.symm m = ⟨m⟩

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.val_add
declarations.statement: lemma val_add (q1 q2 : QuarkDoublet) : (q1 + q2).val = q1.val + q2.val

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.val_smul
declarations.statement: lemma val_smul (r : ℂ) (q : QuarkDoublet) : (r • q).val = r • q.val

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.repLorentzGroup
declarations.doc: The representation of the Lorentz group on the space of quark fields.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def repLorentzGroup : Representation ℂ (SL(2,ℂ)) QuarkDoublet

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.repGaugeGroupI
declarations.doc: The action of the full Standard Model gauge group on quark fields.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def repGaugeGroupI : Representation ℂ GaugeGroupI QuarkDoublet

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.repGaugeGroupI_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_tmul (g : GaugeGroupI) (ψ : Fermion.LeftHandedWeyl)
    (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 3)) (w : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 2)) :
    repGaugeGroupI g ⟨ψ ⊗ₜ v ⊗ₜ w⟩ = ⟨g.toU1 • ψ ⊗ₜ (g.toSU3.1.toEuclideanLin v) ⊗ₜ
      (g.toSU2.1.toEuclideanLin w)⟩

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.repGaugeGroupI_tmul_basis_eq_sum
declarations.doc:
The action of the full gauge group on a tensor product of basis elements, expanded as a
sum over the columns of the `SU(3)` and `SU(2)` matrices.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_tmul_basis_eq_sum (g : GaugeGroupI) (k : Fin 2) (i : Fin 3) (j : Fin 2) :
    repGaugeGroupI g ⟨LeftHandedWeyl.basis k ⊗ₜ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin 3) ℂ i
      ⊗ₜ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin 2) ℂ j⟩ =
      ∑ i' : Fin 3, ∑ j' : Fin 2, (g.toU1.1 * g.toSU3.1 i' i * g.toSU2.1 j' j)
      • (⟨LeftHandedWeyl.basis k ⊗ₜ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin 3) ℂ i'
          ⊗ₜ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin 2) ℂ j'⟩ : QuarkDoublet)

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.repGaugeGroupI_eq_iff_mul_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_eq_iff_mul_eq {g1 g2 : GaugeGroupI} :
    repGaugeGroupI g1 = repGaugeGroupI g2 ↔ ∀ i i' j j',
    g1.toU1.1 * g1.toSU3.1 i' i * g1.toSU2.1 j' j =
    g2.toU1.1 * g2.toSU3.1 i' i * g2.toSU2.1 j' j

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.mem_repGaugeGroupI_ker_iff_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_repGaugeGroupI_ker_iff_eq {g : GaugeGroupI} :
    g ∈ repGaugeGroupI.ker ↔ ∃ a b : ℂ, g.toSU2.1 = a • 1 ∧ g.toSU3.1 = b • 1 ∧
      a * b * g.toU1.1 = 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.gaugeGroup_subgroup_ℤ₆_le_ker_repGaugeGroupI
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeGroup_subgroup_ℤ₆_le_ker_repGaugeGroupI :
    GaugeGroupQuot.subgroup .ℤ₆ ≤ repGaugeGroupI.ker

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.gaugeGroup_subgroup_le_ker_repGaugeGroupI
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeGroup_subgroup_le_ker_repGaugeGroupI (Q : GaugeGroupQuot) :
    Q.subgroup ≤ repGaugeGroupI.ker

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.repGaugeGroup
declarations.doc:
The action of the Standard Model gauge group, potentially quotiented by
a discrete factor on quark fields.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def repGaugeGroup : (Q : GaugeGroupQuot) →
    Representation ℂ (GaugeGroup Q) QuarkDoublet

In this module we define the type corresponding to
the target vector space of an up-type singlet quark field in the Standard Model.

On this type we define a representation of the Lorentz group, and a
representation of the Standard Model gauge group.

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.repGaugeGroupI_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_tmul (g : GaugeGroupI) (ψ : Fermion.RightHandedWeyl)
    (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 3)) :
    repGaugeGroupI g ⟨ψ ⊗ₜ v⟩ = ⟨g.toU1 ^ 4 • ψ ⊗ₜ (g.toSU3.1.toEuclideanLin v)⟩

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.repGaugeGroupI_tmul_basis_eq_sum
declarations.doc:
The action of the full gauge group on a tensor product of basis elements, expanded as a
sum over the columns of the `SU(3)` matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_tmul_basis_eq_sum (g : GaugeGroupI) (k : Fin 2) (i : Fin 3) :

      ∑ i' : Fin 3, (g.toU1.1 ^ 4  * g.toSU3.1 i' i)
      • (⟨RightHandedWeyl.basis k ⊗ₜ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin 3) ℂ i'⟩ : UpSinglet)

lemma mem_repGaugeGroupI_ker_iff_eq {g : GaugeGroupI} :

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeGroupI
declarations.doc:
The global gauge group of the Standard Model with no discrete quotients.
The `I` in the Name is an indication of the statement that this has no discrete quotients.

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeGroupI.diagSU2
declarations.doc:
The diagonal element `diag(a, ā)` of `SU(2)` associated with a phase `a`.
These elements form a maximal torus of `SU(2)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def diagSU2 : unitary ℂ →* specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeGroupI.diagSU2_coe
declarations.statement:
lemma diagSU2_coe (a : unitary ℂ) :
    (diagSU2 a : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) = !![(a : ℂ), 0; 0, (star a : ℂ)]

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeGroupI.eq_diagSU2_of_apply_zero_one_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
An element of `SU(2)` whose upper-right entry vanishes and whose lower-right entry is `w̄`,
for a phase `w`, is the diagonal element `diag(w, w̄)`.

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeGroupI.electromagnetismU1
declarations.doc:
The electromagnetic `U(1)`: the embedding of `U(1)` into the gauge group given by
`u ↦ (1, diag(u³, ū³), u)`, trivial on `SU(3)`. It is generated by the electric charge
`Q = T₃ + Y`, in the normalisation `6Q = 6T₃ + 6Y` where the hypercharges `6Y` are integers.
It is the subgroup left unbroken by a Higgs vacuum of the form `(0, v)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def electromagnetismU1 : unitary ℂ →* GaugeGroupI

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeGroupI.electromagnetismU1_toSU3
declarations.statement:
lemma electromagnetismU1_toSU3 (u1 : unitary ℂ) :
    toSU3 (electromagnetismU1 u1) = 1

declarations.statement:
lemma electromagnetismU1_toSU2 (u1 : unitary ℂ) :
    toSU2 (electromagnetismU1 u1) = diagSU2 (u1 ^ 3)

declarations.statement:
lemma electromagnetismU1_toU1 (u1 : unitary ℂ) :
    toU1 (electromagnetismU1 u1) = u1

The subgroup of the un-quotiented gauge group which acts trivially on all particles in the
standard model, i.e., the ℤ₆-subgroup of `GaugeGroupI` with elements `(α^2 * I₃, α^(-3) * I₂, α)`,

lemma mem_gaugeGroupℤ₆SubGroup_iff (g : GaugeGroupI) :
    g ∈ gaugeGroupℤ₆SubGroup ↔ ∃ α : rootsOfUnity 6 ℂ, gaugeGroupℤ₆OfRoot α = g

declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeGroupℤ₂Hom_apply (α : rootsOfUnity 2 ℂ) :

declarations.statement:

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeGroupQuot.quotientMap_eq_iff
declarations.doc:

modules.title: The unbroken gauge group
modules.doc:
We define the gauge group `SU(3) × U(1)_EM` left unbroken by the Higgs vacuum.

## i. Overview

A non-zero Higgs vacuum breaks `SU(3) × SU(2) × U(1)` down to color and electromagnetism,
`SU(3) × U(1)_EM`. This file defines that group and its inclusion into `GaugeGroupI`.

## ii. Key results

- `UnbrokenGaugeGroupI`: The group `SU(3) × U(1)_EM`.
- `UnbrokenGaugeGroupI.incl`: Its inclusion `(h, u) ↦ (h, diag(u³, ū³), u)` into `GaugeGroupI`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The unbroken gauge group

## iv. References

* Peskin & Schroeder, An Introduction to QFT, chapter 20. [ref: peskin_schroeder_qft]

modules.title: The Higgs field
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The Higgs field describes is the underlying field of the Higgs boson.
It is a map from SpaceTime to a 2-dimensional complex vector space.
In this module we define the Higgs field and prove some basic properties.

## ii. Key results

- `HiggsVec`: The 2-dimensional complex vector space which is the target space of the Higgs field.
  This vector space is equipped with an action of the global gauge group of the Standard Model.
- `HiggsBundle`: The trivial vector bundle over `SpaceTime` with fiber `HiggsVec`.
- `HiggsField`: The type of smooth sections of the `HiggsBundle`, i.e., the type of Higgs fields.
- `stabilizer_ofReal`: The stability group of the Higgs vacuum `(0, √a)`, i.e. the gauge
  group left unbroken by it, is `SU(3) × U(1)_EM`.

## iii. Table of contents

sections.text:
## A. The Higgs vector space

The target space of the Higgs field is a 2-dimensional complex vector space.
In this section we will define this vector space, and the action of the
global gauge group on it.
### A.1. Definition of the Higgs vector space

### A.2. Orthonormal basis

We define an orthonormal basis of `HiggsVec`.

### A.3. Generating Higgs vectors from real numbers

Given a real number `a` we define the Higgs vector corresponding to that real number
as `(0, √a)`. This has the property that its norm-squared is equal to `a`.
Following the textbook convention, the non-zero entry sits in the second (lower) component,
which is the electrically neutral component of the Higgs doublet
(see `GaugeGroupI.electromagnetismU1`).

### A.4. Action of the gauge group on `HiggsVec`

The gauge group of the Standard Model acts on `HiggsVec` by matrix multiplication.
#### A.4.1. Definition of the representation

#### A.4.2. Unitary nature of the action

The action of `StandardModel.GaugeGroupI` on `HiggsVec` is unitary.
#### A.4.3. Group properties of the representation applied to vectors

### A.5. The Gauge orbit of a Higgs vector

We show that two Higgs vectors are in the same gauge orbit if and only if they have the same norm.

#### A.5.1. The rotation matrix to ofReal

We define an element of `GaugeGroupI` which takes a given Higgs vector to the
corresponding `ofReal` Higgs vector.

#### A.5.2. Members of orbits

Members of the orbit of a Higgs vector under the action of `GaugeGroupI` are exactly those
Higgs vectors with the same norm.

### A.6. The stability group of a Higgs vector

The stability group of a Higgs vector `φ` is the subgroup `repGaugeGroupI.stabilizer φ` of
`GaugeGroupI` fixing `φ`, i.e. the gauge group left unbroken when the Higgs field takes the
value `φ`. For the vacuum `ofReal a = (0, √a)` with `a > 0` it is `SU(3) × U(1)_EM`, and for
any other non-zero Higgs vector it is a conjugate of this subgroup. The subgroup fixing every
Higgs vector is `SU(3) × ℤ₆`.
### A.7. The electromagnetic U(1) and the phase of the first component
### A.8. To real scalars

## B. The Higgs bundle

We define the Higgs bundle as the trivial vector bundle with base `SpaceTime` and fiber `HiggsVec`.
The Higgs field will then be defined as smooth sections of this bundle.

### B.1. Definition of the Higgs bundle

We define the Higgs bundle.

### B.2. Instance of a vector bundle

We given the Higgs bundle an instance of a smooth vector bundle.

## C. The Higgs fields

Higgs fields are smooth sections of the Higgs bundle.
This corresponds to smooth maps from `SpaceTime` to `HiggsVec`.
We here define the type of Higgs fields and create an API around them.
### C.1. Relations between `HiggsField` and `HiggsVec`

#### C.1.1. The constant Higgs field

We define the constant Higgs field associated to a given Higgs vector.
#### C.1.2. The map from `HiggsField` to `SpaceTime → HiggsVec`

### C.2. Smoothness properties of components

We prove some smoothness properties of the components of a Higgs field.

### C.3. The pointwise inner product

The pointwise inner product on the Higgs field.
#### C.3.1. Basic equalities
#### C.3.2. Symmetry properties
#### C.3.3. Linearity conditions
#### C.3.4. Smoothness of the inner product

### C.4. The pointwise norm

We define the pointwise norm-squared of a Higgs field.
#### C.4.1. Basic equalities
#### C.4.2. Positivity
#### C.4.3. On the zero section
#### C.4.4. Smoothness of the norm-squared
