declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec
declarations.doc:
The vector space `HiggsVec` is defined to be the complex Euclidean space of dimension 2.
For a given spacetime point a Higgs field gives a value in `HiggsVec`.
declarations.statement: abbrev HiggsVec

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.orthonormBasis
declarations.doc: An orthonormal basis of `HiggsVec`.
declarations.statement: def orthonormBasis : OrthonormalBasis (Fin 2) ℂ HiggsVec

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.ofReal
declarations.doc:
Generating a Higgs vector `(0, √a)` from a real number `a`, such that the norm-squared of
that Higgs vector is `a`.
declarations.statement: def ofReal (a : ℝ) : HiggsVec

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.ofReal_normSq
declarations.statement: lemma ofReal_normSq {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) : ‖ofReal a‖ ^ 2 = a

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.repGaugeGroupI
declarations.doc:
The representation of the gauge group `GaugeGroupI` on `HiggsVec`: the `SU(2)`
factor acts by matrix multiplication, and the `U(1)` factor by scalar
multiplication with its third power. Hypercharges are normalised as `6Y`, so the
power `3` corresponds to the textbook hypercharge `Y = 1/2`.
declarations.statement: def repGaugeGroupI : Representation ℂ GaugeGroupI HiggsVec

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.repGaugeGroupI_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_apply (g : StandardModel.GaugeGroupI) (φ : HiggsVec) :
    repGaugeGroupI g φ = (WithLp.toLp 2 <| g.toU1 ^ 3 • (g.toSU2.1 *ᵥ φ.ofLp))

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.repGaugeGroupI_apply_eq_U1_mul_SU2
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_apply_eq_U1_mul_SU2 (g : StandardModel.GaugeGroupI) (φ : HiggsVec) :
    repGaugeGroupI g φ = (WithLp.toLp 2 <| g.toSU2.1 *ᵥ (g.toU1 ^ 3 • φ.ofLp))

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.repGaugeGroupI_apply_eq_U1_smul_SU2
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_apply_eq_U1_smul_SU2 (g : StandardModel.GaugeGroupI) (φ : HiggsVec) :
    repGaugeGroupI g φ = (WithLp.toLp 2 <| (g.toU1 ^ 3 • g.toSU2.1) *ᵥ φ.ofLp)

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.repGaugeGroupI_inner
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_inner (g : StandardModel.GaugeGroupI) (φ ψ : HiggsVec) :
    ⟪repGaugeGroupI g φ, repGaugeGroupI g ψ⟫_ℂ = ⟪φ, ψ⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.repGaugeGroupI_norm
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_norm (g : StandardModel.GaugeGroupI) (φ : HiggsVec) :
    ‖repGaugeGroupI g φ‖ = ‖φ‖

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.repGaugeGroupI_mul_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_mul_apply (g₁ g₂ : StandardModel.GaugeGroupI) (φ : HiggsVec) :
    repGaugeGroupI (g₁ * g₂) φ = repGaugeGroupI g₁ (repGaugeGroupI g₂ φ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.repGaugeGroupI_inv_apply_eq_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_inv_apply_eq_iff (g : StandardModel.GaugeGroupI) (φ ψ : HiggsVec) :
    repGaugeGroupI g⁻¹ φ = ψ ↔ φ = repGaugeGroupI g ψ

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.toRealGroupElem
declarations.doc:
Given a Higgs vector, a rotation matrix which puts the first component of the
vector to zero, and the second component to a non-negative real.
declarations.statement: def toRealGroupElem (φ : HiggsVec) : GaugeGroupI

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.toRealGroupElem_apply_self
declarations.statement:
lemma toRealGroupElem_apply_self (φ : HiggsVec) :
    repGaugeGroupI (toRealGroupElem φ) φ = ofReal (‖φ‖ ^ 2)

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.exists_repGaugeGroupI_eq_iff_norm_eq
declarations.doc:
Two Higgs vectors are in the same gauge orbit (i.e. related by `repGaugeGroupI`)
if and only if they have the same norm.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_repGaugeGroupI_eq_iff_norm_eq (φ : HiggsVec) (ψ : HiggsVec) :
    (∃ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI g φ = ψ) ↔ ‖ψ‖ = ‖φ‖

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.mem_stabilizer_ofReal_iff
declarations.doc:
A gauge transformation fixes the non-zero Higgs vector `ofReal a = (0, √a)` if and only if
its `SU(2)` part is `diag(u³, ū³)`, where `u` is its `U(1)` part.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_stabilizer_ofReal_iff {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (g : GaugeGroupI) :
    g ∈ repGaugeGroupI.stabilizer (ofReal a) ↔
    GaugeGroupI.toSU2 g = GaugeGroupI.diagSU2 (GaugeGroupI.toU1 g ^ 3)

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.stabilizer_ofReal
declarations.doc:
The Higgs vacuum breaks electroweak symmetry down to color and electromagnetism: the
stability group of the non-zero Higgs vector `ofReal a = (0, √a)` is the subgroup
`SU(3) × U(1)_EM` of `GaugeGroupI`, with elements `(h, diag(u³, ū³), u)`.
declarations.statement:
theorem stabilizer_ofReal {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) :
    repGaugeGroupI.stabilizer (ofReal a) = UnbrokenGaugeGroupI.incl.range

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.exists_stabilizer_eq_conj_unbrokenGaugeGroupI
declarations.doc: The stability group of any non-zero Higgs vector is conjugate to `SU(3) × U(1)_EM`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_stabilizer_eq_conj_unbrokenGaugeGroupI (φ : HiggsVec) (hφ : φ ≠ 0) :
    ∃ g : GaugeGroupI, repGaugeGroupI.stabilizer φ =
      UnbrokenGaugeGroupI.incl.range.map (MulAut.conj g)

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.mem_iInf_stabilizer_iff
declarations.doc:
The gauge transformations fixing every Higgs vector are those of the form
`(h, α⁻³ I₂, α)` with `h ∈ SU(3)` arbitrary and `α` a sixth root of unity, i.e. the subgroup
`SU(3) × ℤ₆` of `GaugeGroupI`. Here `ℤ₆` sits inside `SU(2) × U(1)`: it is the image there of
the central `ℤ₆` used for `GaugeGroupℤ₆`, whose elements also carry the `SU(3)` part `α² I₃`,
so this subgroup contains the central `ℤ₆`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_iInf_stabilizer_iff (g : GaugeGroupI) :
    g ∈ ⨅ φ, repGaugeGroupI.stabilizer φ ↔
    ∃ α : rootsOfUnity 6 ℂ, GaugeGroupI.toSU2 g = gaugeGroupℤ₆SU2OfRoot α ∧
      GaugeGroupI.toU1 g = gaugeGroupℤ₆UnitaryOfRoot α

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.electromagnetismU1_repGaugeGroupI_apply
declarations.doc:
The electromagnetic `U(1)` acts on a Higgs vector as `diag(u⁶, 1)`: the upper component
has electric charge `+1` and the lower component is neutral.
declarations.statement:
lemma electromagnetismU1_repGaugeGroupI_apply (g : unitary ℂ) (φ : HiggsVec) :
    repGaugeGroupI (StandardModel.GaugeGroupI.electromagnetismU1 g) φ =
    (WithLp.toLp 2 <| !![g.1 ^ 6, 0; 0, 1] *ᵥ φ.ofLp)

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.electromagnetismU1_repGaugeGroupI_ofReal
declarations.doc:
The electromagnetic `U(1)` leaves the Higgs vector `ofReal a = (0, √a)` invariant:
the Higgs vacuum is electrically neutral, so electromagnetism is unbroken.
declarations.statement:
lemma electromagnetismU1_repGaugeGroupI_ofReal (g : unitary ℂ) (a : ℝ) :
    repGaugeGroupI (StandardModel.GaugeGroupI.electromagnetismU1 g) (ofReal a) = ofReal a

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.exists_electromagnetismU1_fst_eq_norm
declarations.doc:
There is an element of the electromagnetic `U(1)` making the first (charged) component of a
Higgs vector real and non-negative. It fixes second components, and so the Higgs vacuum
`ofReal a`. This is used to gauge-fix two-Higgs-doublet configurations to
`Φ1 = (0, ‖Φ1‖)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_electromagnetismU1_fst_eq_norm (φ : HiggsVec) :
    ∃ g : unitary ℂ,
      (repGaugeGroupI (StandardModel.GaugeGroupI.electromagnetismU1 g) φ).ofLp 0 = ‖φ.ofLp 0‖

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.toRealScalars
declarations.doc: The underlying real values of the Higgs vector.
declarations.statement: def toRealScalars : HiggsVec →ₗ[ℝ] (Fin 4 → ℝ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.toRealScalars_smul_real
declarations.statement:
lemma toRealScalars_smul_real (a : ℝ) (φ : HiggsVec) :
    toRealScalars (a • φ) = a • toRealScalars φ

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.ofReal_toRealScalars
declarations.statement:
lemma ofReal_toRealScalars (a : ℝ) :
    toRealScalars (ofReal a) = !₄[0, 0, Real.sqrt a, 0]

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsVec.ofReal_toRealScalars_norm
declarations.statement:
lemma ofReal_toRealScalars_norm (φ : HiggsVec) :
    toRealScalars (ofReal (‖φ‖ ^ 2)) = !₄[0, 0, ‖φ‖, 0]

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsBundle
declarations.doc:
The `HiggsBundle` is defined as the trivial vector bundle with base `SpaceTime` and
fiber `HiggsVec`. Thus as a manifold it corresponds to `ℝ⁴ × ℂ²`.
declarations.statement: abbrev HiggsBundle

declarations.doc: The instance of a smooth vector bundle with total space `HiggsBundle` and fiber `HiggsVec`.
declarations.statement: instance : ContMDiffVectorBundle ⊤ HiggsVec HiggsBundle (Lorentz.Vector.asSmoothManifold 3)

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField
declarations.doc:
The type `HiggsField` is defined such that elements are smooth sections of the trivial
vector bundle `HiggsBundle`. Such elements are Higgs fields. Since `HiggsField` is
trivial as a vector bundle, a Higgs field is equivalent to a smooth map
from `SpaceTime` to `HiggsVec`.
declarations.statement: abbrev HiggsField : Type

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.const
declarations.doc:
Given a vector in `HiggsVec` the constant Higgs field with value equal to that
section.
declarations.statement: def const : HiggsVec →ₗ[ℝ] HiggsField

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.const_apply
declarations.doc:
For all spacetime points, the constant Higgs field defined by a Higgs vector,
returns that Higgs Vector.
declarations.statement: lemma const_apply (φ : HiggsVec) (x : SpaceTime) : const φ x = φ

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.toHiggsVec
declarations.doc: Given a `HiggsField`, the corresponding map from `SpaceTime` to `HiggsVec`.
declarations.statement: def toHiggsVec (φ : HiggsField) : SpaceTime → HiggsVec

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.toHiggsVec_smooth
declarations.statement:
lemma toHiggsVec_smooth (φ : HiggsField) :
    ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, SpaceTime) 𝓘(ℝ, HiggsVec) ⊤ φ.toHiggsVec

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.const_toHiggsVec_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma const_toHiggsVec_apply (φ : HiggsField) (x : SpaceTime) :
    const (φ.toHiggsVec x) x = φ x

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.contDiff
declarations.statement:
lemma contDiff (φ : HiggsField) :
    ContDiff ℝ ⊤ φ

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.toVec_smooth
declarations.statement:
lemma toVec_smooth (φ : HiggsField) :
    ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, SpaceTime) 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 2)) ⊤ φ

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.apply_smooth
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_smooth (φ : HiggsField) :
    ∀ i, ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, SpaceTime) 𝓘(ℝ, ℂ) ⊤ (fun (x : SpaceTime) => (φ x i))

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.apply_re_smooth
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_re_smooth (φ : HiggsField) (i : Fin 2) :
    ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, SpaceTime) 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) ⊤ (reCLM ∘ (fun (x : SpaceTime) => (φ x i)))

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.apply_im_smooth
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_im_smooth (φ : HiggsField) (i : Fin 2) :
    ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, SpaceTime) 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) ⊤ (imCLM ∘ (fun (x : SpaceTime) => (φ x i)))
instance : Inner (SpaceTime → ℂ) (HiggsField)

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.inner_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_apply (φ1 φ2 : HiggsField) (x : SpaceTime) :
    ⟪φ1, φ2⟫_(SpaceTime → ℂ) x = ⟪φ1 x, φ2 x⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.inner_eq_expand
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_eq_expand (φ1 φ2 : HiggsField) :
    ⟪φ1, φ2⟫_(SpaceTime → ℂ) = fun x => equivRealProdCLM.symm (((φ1 x 0).re * (φ2 x 0).re
    + (φ1 x 1).re * (φ2 x 1).re+ (φ1 x 0).im * (φ2 x 0).im + (φ1 x 1).im * (φ2 x 1).im),
    ((φ1 x 0).re * (φ2 x 0).im + (φ1 x 1).re * (φ2 x 1).im
    - (φ1 x 0).im * (φ2 x 0).re - (φ1 x 1).im * (φ2 x 1).re))

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.inner_expand_conj
declarations.doc:
Expands the inner product on Higgs fields in terms of complex components of the
Higgs fields.
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_expand_conj (φ1 φ2 : HiggsField) (x : SpaceTime) :
    ⟪φ1, φ2⟫_(SpaceTime → ℂ) x = conj (φ1 x 0) * φ2 x 0 + conj (φ1 x 1) * φ2 x 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.inner_symm
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_symm (φ1 φ2 : HiggsField) :
    conj ⟪φ2, φ1⟫_(SpaceTime → ℂ) = ⟪φ1, φ2⟫_(SpaceTime → ℂ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.inner_add_left
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_add_left (φ1 φ2 φ3 : HiggsField) :
    ⟪φ1 + φ2, φ3⟫_(SpaceTime → ℂ) = ⟪φ1, φ3⟫_(SpaceTime → ℂ) + ⟪φ2, φ3⟫_(SpaceTime → ℂ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.inner_add_right
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_add_right (φ1 φ2 φ3 : HiggsField) :
    ⟪φ1, φ2 + φ3⟫_(SpaceTime → ℂ) = ⟪φ1, φ2⟫_(SpaceTime → ℂ) + ⟪φ1, φ3⟫_(SpaceTime → ℂ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.inner_zero_left
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_zero_left (φ : HiggsField) :
    ⟪0, φ⟫_(SpaceTime → ℂ) = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.inner_zero_right
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_zero_right (φ : HiggsField) :
    ⟪φ, 0⟫_(SpaceTime → ℂ) = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.inner_neg_left
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_neg_left (φ1 φ2 : HiggsField) :
    ⟪-φ1, φ2⟫_(SpaceTime → ℂ) = -⟪φ1, φ2⟫_(SpaceTime → ℂ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.inner_neg_right
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_neg_right (φ1 φ2 : HiggsField) :
    ⟪φ1, -φ2⟫_(SpaceTime → ℂ) = -⟪φ1, φ2⟫_(SpaceTime → ℂ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.inner_smooth
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_smooth (φ1 φ2 : HiggsField) : ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, SpaceTime) 𝓘(ℝ, ℂ) ⊤
    ⟪φ1, φ2⟫_(SpaceTime → ℂ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.normSq
declarations.doc:
Given an element `φ` of `HiggsField`, `normSq φ` is defined as the
the function `SpaceTime → ℝ` obtained by taking the square norm of the
pointwise Higgs vector. In other words, `normSq φ x = ‖φ x‖ ^ 2`.

The notation `‖φ‖_H^2` is used for the `normSq φ`.
declarations.statement: def normSq (φ : HiggsField) : SpaceTime → ℝ

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.inner_self_eq_normSq
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_self_eq_normSq (φ : HiggsField) (x : SpaceTime) :
    ⟪φ, φ⟫_(SpaceTime → ℂ) x = ‖φ‖_H^2 x

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.normSq_eq_inner_self_re
declarations.statement:
lemma normSq_eq_inner_self_re (φ : HiggsField) (x : SpaceTime) :
    φ.normSq x = (⟪φ, φ⟫_(SpaceTime → ℂ) x).re

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.normSq_expand
declarations.doc: The expansion of the norm squared of into components.
declarations.statement:
lemma normSq_expand (φ : HiggsField) :
    φ.normSq = fun x => (conj (φ x 0) * (φ x 0) + conj (φ x 1) * (φ x 1)).re

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.normSq_nonneg
declarations.statement: lemma normSq_nonneg (φ : HiggsField) (x : SpaceTime) : 0 ≤ ‖φ‖_H^2 x

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.normSq_zero
declarations.statement: lemma normSq_zero : ‖0‖_H^2 = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.normSq_smooth
declarations.doc: The norm squared of the Higgs field is a smooth function on space-time.
declarations.statement: lemma normSq_smooth (φ : HiggsField) : ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, SpaceTime) 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) ⊤ φ.normSq

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.const_normSq
declarations.statement:
lemma const_normSq (φ : HiggsVec) (x : SpaceTime) :
    ‖const φ‖_H^2 x = ‖φ‖ ^ 2

modules.title: The effective potential of the Higgs field
modules.doc:
We define a general effective potential for the Higgs field.
For this we define two properties of the potential: invariance under the gauge group, and a
maximum mass dimension.

Given these, we prove that the potential can be expressed as a polynomial in the norm of the
Higgs field.

sections.text: ## A. The invariance of the general potential under the gauge group
## B. Maximum mass dimension
## C. Terms of a given mass dimension
## D. Potential in terms of the norm of the Higgs field

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential
declarations.doc: A general potential of the Higgs field.
declarations.statement: abbrev EffectivePotential : Type

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.IsInvariant
declarations.doc:
The proposition that the general potential is invariant under
the global action of the gauge group.
declarations.statement: def IsInvariant (V : EffectivePotential) : Prop

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.IsInvariant.eq_on_orbits
declarations.doc: An invariant potential is equal on gauge orbits.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_on_orbits {φ1 φ2 : HiggsVec} {V : EffectivePotential} (h : IsInvariant V)
    (hφ : ∃ g : GaugeGroupI, HiggsVec.repGaugeGroupI g φ2 = φ1) :
    V φ1 = V φ2

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.IsInvariant.eq_of_norm_eq
declarations.doc: An invariant potential is equal on Higgs vectors with identical norms.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_of_norm_eq {φ1 φ2 : HiggsVec} {V : EffectivePotential} (h : IsInvariant V)
    (hφ : ‖φ1‖ = ‖φ2‖) :
    V φ1 = V φ2

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.IsInvariant.factors_through_norm
declarations.statement:
lemma factors_through_norm {V : EffectivePotential} (h : IsInvariant V) :
    ∃ (f : ℝ → ℝ), V = f ∘ norm

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.HasMaxMassDimLE
declarations.doc:
The proposition that the potential `V` has a maximum mass dimension
less then or equal to `n` - also implying it is a polynomial.
declarations.statement: def HasMaxMassDimLE (V : EffectivePotential) (n : ℕ) : Prop

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.polynomial
declarations.doc:
The polynomial associated to a potential `V` with a maximum mass dimension
less than or equal to `n`.
declarations.statement:
def polynomial (V : EffectivePotential) {n : ℕ} (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n) :
    MvPolynomial (Fin 4) ℝ

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.polynomial_totalDegree
declarations.statement:
lemma polynomial_totalDegree {V : EffectivePotential} {n : ℕ} (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n) :
    (polynomial V h).totalDegree ≤ n

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.apply_eq_polynomial
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_eq_polynomial {V : EffectivePotential} {n : ℕ} (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n)
    (φ : HiggsVec) : V φ = (polynomial V h).eval φ.toRealScalars

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.termOfMassDim
declarations.doc: The part of a potential at a given mass-dimension.
declarations.statement:
def termOfMassDim (V : EffectivePotential) {n : ℕ} (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n) (m : ℕ) :
    HiggsVec → ℝ

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.termOfMassDim_eq_zero_of_max_lt
declarations.statement:
lemma termOfMassDim_eq_zero_of_max_lt {V : EffectivePotential} {n : ℕ} (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n)
    {m : ℕ} (hm : n < m) (φ : HiggsVec) :
    termOfMassDim V h m φ = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.termOfMassDim_homogeneity
declarations.statement:
lemma termOfMassDim_homogeneity {V : EffectivePotential} {n : ℕ} (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n) (m : ℕ)
    (φ : HiggsVec) (t : ℝ) : termOfMassDim V h m (t • φ) = t ^ m * termOfMassDim V h m φ

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.apply_eq_sum_termOfMassDim
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_eq_sum_termOfMassDim {V : EffectivePotential} {n : ℕ} (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n)
    (φ : HiggsVec) :
    V φ = ∑ m ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), termOfMassDim V h m φ

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.apply_smul_eq_sum_termOfMassDim
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_smul_eq_sum_termOfMassDim {V : EffectivePotential} {n : ℕ} (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n)
    (φ : HiggsVec) (t : ℝ) :
    V (t • φ) = ∑ m ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), t ^ m * termOfMassDim V h m φ

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.termOfMassDim_isInvariant
declarations.statement:
lemma termOfMassDim_isInvariant {V : EffectivePotential} {n : ℕ} (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n)
    (m : ℕ) (hV : IsInvariant V) : IsInvariant (termOfMassDim V h m)

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.termOfMassDim_eq_mul_norm
StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.termOfMassDim_zero_of_odd
declarations.statement:
lemma termOfMassDim_zero_of_odd {V : EffectivePotential} {n : ℕ} (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n) (m : ℕ)
    (hV : IsInvariant V) (φ : HiggsVec) (hodd : Odd m)  :
    termOfMassDim V h m φ = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.apply_eq_sum_even_termOfMassDim
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_eq_sum_even_termOfMassDim {V : EffectivePotential} {n : ℕ} (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n)
    (hV : IsInvariant V) (φ : HiggsVec) :
    V φ = ∑ m ∈ Finset.range (n / 2 + 1), termOfMassDim V h (2 * m) φ

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.apply_eq_sum_even_termOfMassDim_fin
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_eq_sum_even_termOfMassDim_fin {V : EffectivePotential} {n : ℕ} (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n)
    (hV : IsInvariant V) (φ : HiggsVec) :
    V φ = ∑ m : Fin (n/2 + 1), termOfMassDim V h (2 * m) φ

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.EffectivePotential.apply_eq_sum_norm_pow
declarations.doc: The potential is equal to the sum of norms to even powers.
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_eq_sum_norm_pow {V : EffectivePotential} {n : ℕ} (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n)
    (hV : IsInvariant V) (φ : HiggsVec) :
    ∃ c : Fin (n/2 + 1) → ℝ, V φ = ∑ m, c m • ‖φ‖ ^ (2 * m.1)

modules.title: The potential of the Higgs field
modules.doc:
We define the potential of the Higgs field.

We show that the potential is a smooth function on spacetime.

sections.text: ## The Higgs potential
## Basic properties
## The discriminant
## Boundedness of the potential
## Minimum and maximum

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential
declarations.doc:
The structure `Potential` is defined with two fields, `μ2` corresponding
to the mass-squared of the Higgs boson, and `l` corresponding to the coefficient
of the quartic term in the Higgs potential. Note that `l` is usually denoted `λ`.
declarations.statement:
structure Potential where
  /-- The mass-squared of the Higgs boson. -/
  μ2 : ℝ
  /-- The quartic coupling of the Higgs boson. Usually denoted λ. -/
  𝓵 : ℝ

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.toFun
declarations.doc:
Given a element `P` of `Potential`, `P.toFun` is Higgs potential.
It is defined for a Higgs field `φ` and a spacetime point `x` as

`-μ² ‖φ‖_H^2 x + l * ‖φ‖_H^2 x * ‖φ‖_H^2 x`.
declarations.statement: def toFun (φ : HiggsField) (x : SpaceTime) : ℝ

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.toFun_smooth
declarations.doc: The potential is smooth.
declarations.statement:
lemma toFun_smooth (φ : HiggsField) :
    ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, SpaceTime) 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) ⊤ (fun x => P.toFun φ x)

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.neg
declarations.doc: The Higgs potential formed by negating the mass squared and the quartic coupling.
declarations.statement: def neg : Potential

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.toFun_neg
declarations.statement: lemma toFun_neg (φ : HiggsField) (x : SpaceTime) : P.neg.toFun φ x = - P.toFun φ x

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.μ2_neg
declarations.statement: lemma μ2_neg : P.neg.μ2 = - P.μ2

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.𝓵_neg
declarations.statement: lemma 𝓵_neg : P.neg.𝓵 = - P.𝓵

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.toFun_zero
declarations.statement: lemma toFun_zero (x : SpaceTime) : P.toFun 0 x = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.toFun_eq_of_repGaugeGroupI
declarations.doc:
The Higgs potential is gauge invariant: at a spacetime point `x`, it takes the same value on
two Higgs fields whose values at `x` are related by an element of the gauge group.
declarations.statement:
lemma toFun_eq_of_repGaugeGroupI (g : GaugeGroupI) (φ ψ : HiggsField) (x : SpaceTime)
    (h : ψ x = HiggsVec.repGaugeGroupI g (φ x)) : P.toFun ψ x = P.toFun φ x

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.complete_square
declarations.statement:
lemma complete_square (h : P.𝓵 ≠ 0) (φ : HiggsField) (x : SpaceTime) :
    P.toFun φ x = P.𝓵 * (‖φ‖_H^2 x - P.μ2 / (2 * P.𝓵)) ^ 2 - P.μ2 ^ 2 / (4 * P.𝓵)

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.as_quad
declarations.doc: The quadratic equation satisfied by the Higgs potential at a spacetime point `x`.
declarations.statement:
lemma as_quad (φ : HiggsField) (x : SpaceTime) :
    P.𝓵 * ‖φ‖_H^2 x * ‖φ‖_H^2 x + (- P.μ2) * ‖φ‖_H^2 x + (- P.toFun φ x) = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.toFun_eq_zero_iff
declarations.doc:
The Higgs potential is zero iff and only if the higgs field is zero, or the
higgs field has norm-squared `P.μ2 / P.𝓵`, assuming `P.𝓁 = 0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma toFun_eq_zero_iff (h : P.𝓵 ≠ 0) (φ : HiggsField) (x : SpaceTime) :
    P.toFun φ x = 0 ↔ φ x = 0 ∨ ‖φ‖_H^2 x = P.μ2 / P.𝓵

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.quadDiscrim
declarations.doc: The discriminant of the quadratic equation formed by the Higgs potential.
declarations.statement: def quadDiscrim (φ : HiggsField) (x : SpaceTime) : ℝ

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.quadDiscrim_nonneg
declarations.doc: The discriminant of the quadratic formed by the potential is non-negative.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadDiscrim_nonneg (h : P.𝓵 ≠ 0) (φ : HiggsField) (x : SpaceTime) :
    0 ≤ P.quadDiscrim φ x

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.quadDiscrim_eq_sqrt_mul_sqrt
declarations.statement:
lemma quadDiscrim_eq_sqrt_mul_sqrt (h : P.𝓵 ≠ 0) (φ : HiggsField) (x : SpaceTime) :
    P.quadDiscrim φ x = Real.sqrt (P.quadDiscrim φ x) * Real.sqrt (P.quadDiscrim φ x)

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.quadDiscrim_eq_zero_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma quadDiscrim_eq_zero_iff (h : P.𝓵 ≠ 0) (φ : HiggsField) (x : SpaceTime) :
    P.quadDiscrim φ x = 0 ↔ P.toFun φ x = - P.μ2 ^ 2 / (4 * P.𝓵)

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.quadDiscrim_eq_zero_iff_normSq
declarations.statement:
lemma quadDiscrim_eq_zero_iff_normSq (h : P.𝓵 ≠ 0) (φ : HiggsField) (x : SpaceTime) :
    P.quadDiscrim φ x = 0 ↔ ‖φ‖_H^2 x = P.μ2 / (2 * P.𝓵)

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.neg_𝓵_quadDiscrim_zero_bound
declarations.doc:
For an element `P` of `Potential`, if `l < 0` then the following upper bound for the potential
exists

`P.toFun φ x ≤ - μ2 ^ 2 / (4 * 𝓵)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma neg_𝓵_quadDiscrim_zero_bound (h : P.𝓵 < 0) (φ : HiggsField) (x : SpaceTime) :
    P.toFun φ x ≤ - P.μ2 ^ 2 / (4 * P.𝓵)

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.pos_𝓵_quadDiscrim_zero_bound
declarations.doc:
For an element `P` of `Potential`, if `0 < l` then the following lower bound for the potential
exists

`- μ2 ^ 2 / (4 * 𝓵) ≤ P.toFun φ x`.
declarations.statement:
lemma pos_𝓵_quadDiscrim_zero_bound (h : 0 < P.𝓵) (φ : HiggsField) (x : SpaceTime) :
    - P.μ2 ^ 2 / (4 * P.𝓵) ≤ P.toFun φ x

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.neg_𝓵_toFun_neg
declarations.doc:
If `P.𝓵` is negative, then if `P.μ2` is greater than zero, for all space-time points,
the potential is negative `P.toFun φ x ≤ 0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma neg_𝓵_toFun_neg (h : P.𝓵 < 0) (φ : HiggsField) (x : SpaceTime) :
    (0 < P.μ2 ∧ P.toFun φ x ≤ 0) ∨ P.μ2 ≤ 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.pos_𝓵_toFun_pos
declarations.doc:
If `P.𝓵` is bigger then zero, then if `P.μ2` is less than zero, for all space-time points,
the potential is positive `0 ≤ P.toFun φ x`.
declarations.statement:
lemma pos_𝓵_toFun_pos (h : 0 < P.𝓵) (φ : HiggsField) (x : SpaceTime) :
    (P.μ2 < 0 ∧ 0 ≤ P.toFun φ x) ∨ 0 ≤ P.μ2

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.neg_𝓵_sol_exists_iff
declarations.doc:
For an element `P` of `Potential` with `l < 0` and a real `c : ℝ`, there exists
  a Higgs field `φ` and a spacetime point `x` such that `P.toFun φ x = c` iff one of the
  following two conditions hold:
- `0 < μ2` and `c ≤ 0`. That is, if `l` is negative and `μ2` positive, then the potential
  takes every non-positive value.
- or `μ2 ≤ 0` and `c ≤ - μ2 ^ 2 / (4 * 𝓵)`. That is, if `l` is negative and `μ2` non-positive,
  then the potential takes every value less then or equal to its bound.
declarations.statement:
lemma neg_𝓵_sol_exists_iff (h𝓵 : P.𝓵 < 0) (c : ℝ) : (∃ φ x, P.toFun φ x = c) ↔ (0 < P.μ2 ∧ c ≤ 0) ∨
    (P.μ2 ≤ 0 ∧ c ≤ - P.μ2 ^ 2 / (4 * P.𝓵))

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.pos_𝓵_sol_exists_iff
declarations.doc:
For an element `P` of `Potential` with `0 < l` and a real `c : ℝ`, there exists
  a Higgs field `φ` and a spacetime point `x` such that `P.toFun φ x = c` iff one of the
  following two conditions hold:
- `μ2 < 0` and `0 ≤ c`. That is, if `l` is positive and `μ2` negative, then the potential
  takes every non-negative value.
- or `0 ≤ μ2` and `- μ2 ^ 2 / (4 * 𝓵) ≤ c`. That is, if `l` is positive and `μ2` non-negative,
  then the potential takes every value greater then or equal to its bound.
declarations.statement:
lemma pos_𝓵_sol_exists_iff (h𝓵 : 0 < P.𝓵) (c : ℝ) : (∃ φ x, P.toFun φ x = c) ↔ (P.μ2 < 0 ∧ 0 ≤ c) ∨
    (0 ≤ P.μ2 ∧ - P.μ2 ^ 2 / (4 * P.𝓵) ≤ c)

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.IsBounded
declarations.doc:
Given a element `P` of `Potential`, the proposition `IsBounded P` is true if and only if
there exists a real `c` such that for all Higgs fields `φ` and spacetime points `x`,
the Higgs potential corresponding to `φ` at `x` is greater then or equal to`c`. I.e.

`∀ Φ x, c ≤ P.toFun Φ x`.
declarations.statement: def IsBounded : Prop

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.isBounded_𝓵_nonneg
declarations.doc:
Given a element `P` of `Potential` which is bounded,
the quartic coefficient `𝓵` of `P` is non-negative.
declarations.statement: lemma isBounded_𝓵_nonneg (h : P.IsBounded) : 0 ≤ P.𝓵

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.isBounded_of_𝓵_pos
declarations.doc: Given a element `P` of `Potential` with `0 < 𝓵`, then the potential is bounded.
declarations.statement: lemma isBounded_of_𝓵_pos (h : 0 < P.𝓵) : P.IsBounded

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.eq_zero_iff_of_μSq_nonpos_𝓵_pos
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_zero_iff_of_μSq_nonpos_𝓵_pos (h𝓵 : 0 < P.𝓵) (hμ2 : P.μ2 ≤ 0) (φ : HiggsField)
    (x : SpaceTime) : P.toFun φ x = 0 ↔ φ x = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.isMinOn_iff_of_μSq_nonpos_𝓵_pos
declarations.statement:
lemma isMinOn_iff_of_μSq_nonpos_𝓵_pos (h𝓵 : 0 < P.𝓵) (hμ2 : P.μ2 ≤ 0) (φ : HiggsField)
    (x : SpaceTime) : IsMinOn (fun (φ, x) => P.toFun φ x) Set.univ (φ, x)
    ↔ P.toFun φ x = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.isMinOn_iff_field_of_μSq_nonpos_𝓵_pos
declarations.statement:
lemma isMinOn_iff_field_of_μSq_nonpos_𝓵_pos (h𝓵 : 0 < P.𝓵) (hμ2 : P.μ2 ≤ 0) (φ : HiggsField)
    (x : SpaceTime) : IsMinOn (fun (φ, x) => P.toFun φ x) Set.univ (φ, x)
    ↔ φ x = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.isMinOn_iff_of_μSq_nonneg_𝓵_pos
declarations.statement:
lemma isMinOn_iff_of_μSq_nonneg_𝓵_pos (h𝓵 : 0 < P.𝓵) (hμ2 : 0 ≤ P.μ2) (φ : HiggsField)
    (x : SpaceTime) : IsMinOn (fun (φ, x) => P.toFun φ x) Set.univ (φ, x) ↔
    P.toFun φ x = - P.μ2 ^ 2 / (4 * P.𝓵)

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.isMinOn_iff_field_of_μSq_nonneg_𝓵_pos
declarations.statement:
lemma isMinOn_iff_field_of_μSq_nonneg_𝓵_pos (h𝓵 : 0 < P.𝓵) (hμ2 : 0 ≤ P.μ2) (φ : HiggsField)
    (x : SpaceTime) : IsMinOn (fun (φ, x) => P.toFun φ x) Set.univ (φ, x) ↔
    ‖φ‖_H^2 x = P.μ2 /(2 * P.𝓵)

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.isMinOn_iff_field_of_𝓵_pos
declarations.doc:
Given an element `P` of `Potential` with `0 < l`, then the Higgs field `φ` and
  spacetime point `x` minimize the potential if and only if one of the following conditions
  holds
- `0 ≤ μ2` and `‖φ‖_H^2 x = μ2 / (2 * 𝓵)`.
- or `μ2 < 0` and `φ x = 0`.
declarations.statement:
theorem isMinOn_iff_field_of_𝓵_pos (h𝓵 : 0 < P.𝓵) (φ : HiggsField) (x : SpaceTime) :
    IsMinOn (fun (φ, x) => P.toFun φ x) Set.univ (φ, x) ↔
    (0 ≤ P.μ2 ∧ ‖φ‖_H^2 x = P.μ2 /(2 * P.𝓵)) ∨ (P.μ2 < 0 ∧ φ x = 0)

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.isMaxOn_iff_isMinOn_neg
declarations.statement:
lemma isMaxOn_iff_isMinOn_neg (φ : HiggsField) (x : SpaceTime) :
    IsMaxOn (fun (φ, x) => P.toFun φ x) Set.univ (φ, x) ↔
    IsMinOn (fun (φ, x) => P.neg.toFun φ x) Set.univ (φ, x)

declarations.name: StandardModel.HiggsField.Potential.isMaxOn_iff_field_of_𝓵_neg
declarations.doc:
Given an element `P` of `Potential` with `l < 0`, then the Higgs field `φ` and
  spacetime point `x` maximizes the potential if and only if one of the following conditions
  holds
- `μ2 ≤ 0` and `‖φ‖_H^2 x = μ2 / (2 * 𝓵)`.
- or `0 < μ2` and `φ x = 0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isMaxOn_iff_field_of_𝓵_neg (h𝓵 : P.𝓵 < 0) (φ : HiggsField) (x : SpaceTime) :
    IsMaxOn (fun (φ, x) => P.toFun φ x) Set.univ (φ, x) ↔
    (P.μ2 ≤ 0 ∧ ‖φ‖_H^2 x = P.μ2 /(2 * P.𝓵)) ∨ (0 < P.μ2 ∧ φ x = 0)

modules.title: The MSSM with 3 families and RHNs
modules.doc:
We define the system of ACCs for the MSSM with 3 families and RHNs.
We define the system of charges for 1-species. We prove some basic lemmas about them.

declarations.name: MSSMCharges
declarations.doc: The vector space of charges corresponding to the MSSM fermions.
declarations.statement: def MSSMCharges : ACCSystemCharges

declarations.name: MSSMSpecies
declarations.doc: The vector spaces of charges of one species of fermions in the MSSM.
declarations.statement: def MSSMSpecies : ACCSystemCharges

declarations.name: MSSMCharges.sum_MSSMSpecies_numberCharges_eq_expand
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_MSSMSpecies_numberCharges_eq_expand [AddCommMonoid M]
    (f : Fin MSSMSpecies.numberCharges → M) :
    ∑ i, f i = f ⟨0, by simp⟩ + f ⟨1, by simp⟩ + f ⟨2, by simp⟩

declarations.name: MSSMCharges.toSMPlusH
declarations.doc:
An equivalence between `MSSMCharges.charges` and the space of maps
`(Fin 18 ⊕ Fin 2 → ℚ)`. The first 18 factors corresponds to the SM fermions, while the last two
are the higgsions.
declarations.statement: def toSMPlusH : MSSMCharges.Charges ≃ (Fin 18 ⊕ Fin 2 → ℚ)

declarations.name: MSSMCharges.splitSMPlusH
declarations.doc: An equivalence between `Fin 18 ⊕ Fin 2 → ℚ` and `(Fin 18 → ℚ) × (Fin 2 → ℚ)`.
declarations.statement: def splitSMPlusH : (Fin 18 ⊕ Fin 2 → ℚ) ≃ (Fin 18 → ℚ) × (Fin 2 → ℚ)

declarations.name: MSSMCharges.toSplitSMPlusH
declarations.doc:
An equivalence between `MSSMCharges.charges` and `(Fin 18 → ℚ) × (Fin 2 → ℚ)`. This
splits the charges up into the SM and the additional ones for the MSSM.
declarations.statement: def toSplitSMPlusH : MSSMCharges.Charges ≃ (Fin 18 → ℚ) × (Fin 2 → ℚ)

declarations.name: MSSMCharges.toSpeciesMaps'
declarations.doc: An equivalence between `(Fin 18 → ℚ)` and `(Fin 6 → Fin 3 → ℚ)`.
declarations.statement: def toSpeciesMaps' : (Fin 18 → ℚ) ≃ (Fin 6 → Fin 3 → ℚ)

declarations.name: MSSMCharges.toSpecies
declarations.doc:
An equivalence between `MSSMCharges.charges` and `(Fin 6 → Fin 3 → ℚ) × (Fin 2 → ℚ))`.
This splits charges up into the SM and additional fermions, and further splits the SM into
species.
declarations.statement: def toSpecies : MSSMCharges.Charges ≃ (Fin 6 → Fin 3 → ℚ) × (Fin 2 → ℚ)

declarations.name: MSSMCharges.toSMSpecies
declarations.doc:
For a given `i ∈ Fin 6` the projection of `MSSMCharges.charges` down to the
corresponding SM species of charges.
declarations.statement: def toSMSpecies (i : Fin 6) : MSSMCharges.Charges →ₗ[ℚ] MSSMSpecies.Charges

declarations.name: MSSMCharges.toSMSpecies_toSpecies_inv
declarations.statement:
lemma toSMSpecies_toSpecies_inv (i : Fin 6) (f : (Fin 6 → Fin 3 → ℚ) × (Fin 2 → ℚ)) :
    (toSMSpecies i) (toSpecies.symm f) = f.1 i

declarations.statement:
lemma charges_eq_toSpecies_eq (S T : MSSMCharges.Charges) :

declarations.name: MSSMACCs.accCube
declarations.doc: The cubic ACC.
declarations.statement: def accCube : HomogeneousCubic MSSMCharges.Charges

    (hd : Hd S = Hd T) (hu : Hu S = Hu T) :
    accCube S = accCube T

modules.title: The line through B₃ and Y₃
modules.doc:
We give properties of lines through `B₃` and `Y₃`. We show that every point on this line
is a solution to the quadratic `lineY₃B₃Charges_quad` and a double point of the cubic
`lineY₃B₃_doublePoint`.

# References

* The main reference for the material in this file. [ref: Allanach:2021yjy]

declarations.name: MSSMACC.lineY₃B₃Charges

declarations.statement:
lemma lineY₃B₃Charges_val (a b : ℚ) :
    (lineY₃B₃Charges a b).val = a • Y₃.1.1.val + b • B₃.1.1.val

declarations.name: MSSMACC.lineY₃B₃Charges_quad
declarations.statement: lemma lineY₃B₃Charges_quad (a b : ℚ) : accQuad (lineY₃B₃Charges a b).val = 0

declarations.name: MSSMACC.lineY₃B₃Charges_cubic
declarations.statement: lemma lineY₃B₃Charges_cubic (a b : ℚ) : accCube (lineY₃B₃Charges a b).val = 0

declarations.name: MSSMACC.lineY₃B₃_doublePoint

modules.title: The type of solutions perpendicular to `Y₃` and `B₃`
modules.doc:
We define the type of solutions which are orthogonal to `Y₃` and `B₃` and prove some basic lemmas
about them.

# References

* The main reference for the material in this file is https://arxiv.org/pdf/2107.07926.pdf.
  [ref: Allanach:2021yjy]

declarations.name: MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp
declarations.doc: The type of linear solutions orthogonal to $Y_3$ and $B_3$.
declarations.statement:
structure AnomalyFreePerp extends MSSMACC.LinSols where
  perpY₃ : dot Y₃.val val = 0
  perpB₃ : dot B₃.val val = 0

declarations.name: MSSMACC.proj
declarations.doc:
The projection of an object in `MSSMACC.AnomalyFreeLinear` onto the subspace
orthogonal to `Y₃` and`B₃`.
declarations.statement: def proj (T : MSSMACC.LinSols) : MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp

declarations.name: MSSMACC.proj_val
declarations.statement:
lemma proj_val (T : MSSMACC.LinSols) :
    (proj T).val = (dot B₃.val T.val - dot Y₃.val T.val) • Y₃.val +
    (dot Y₃.val T.val - 2 * dot B₃.val T.val) • B₃.val +
    dot Y₃.val B₃.val • T.val

declarations.name: MSSMACC.Y₃_plus_B₃_plus_proj
declarations.statement:
lemma Y₃_plus_B₃_plus_proj (T : MSSMACC.LinSols) (a b c : ℚ) :
    a • Y₃.val + b • B₃.val + c • (proj T).val =
    (a + c * (dot B₃.val T.val - dot Y₃.val T.val)) • Y₃.val
    + (b + c * (dot Y₃.val T.val - 2 * dot B₃.val T.val)) • B₃.val
    + (dot Y₃.val B₃.val * c) • T.val

declarations.name: MSSMACC.quad_Y₃_proj
declarations.statement:
lemma quad_Y₃_proj (T : MSSMACC.LinSols) :
    quadBiLin Y₃.val (proj T).val = dot Y₃.val B₃.val * quadBiLin Y₃.val T.val

declarations.name: MSSMACC.quad_B₃_proj
declarations.statement:
lemma quad_B₃_proj (T : MSSMACC.LinSols) :
    quadBiLin B₃.val (proj T).val = dot Y₃.val B₃.val * quadBiLin B₃.val T.val

declarations.name: MSSMACC.quad_self_proj
declarations.statement:
lemma quad_self_proj (T : MSSMACC.Sols) :
    quadBiLin T.val (proj T.1.1).val =
    (dot B₃.val T.val - dot Y₃.val T.val) * quadBiLin Y₃.val T.val +
    (dot Y₃.val T.val - 2 * dot B₃.val T.val) * quadBiLin B₃.val T.val

declarations.name: MSSMACC.quad_proj
declarations.statement:
lemma quad_proj (T : MSSMACC.Sols) :
    quadBiLin (proj T.1.1).val (proj T.1.1).val = 2 * dot Y₃.val B₃.val *
    ((dot B₃.val T.val - dot Y₃.val T.val) * quadBiLin Y₃.val T.val +
    (dot Y₃.val T.val - 2 * dot B₃.val T.val) * quadBiLin B₃.val T.val)

declarations.name: MSSMACC.cube_proj_proj_Y₃
declarations.statement:
lemma cube_proj_proj_Y₃ (T : MSSMACC.LinSols) :
    cubeTriLin (proj T).val (proj T).val Y₃.val =
    (dot Y₃.val B₃.val)^2 * cubeTriLin T.val T.val Y₃.val

declarations.name: MSSMACC.cube_proj_proj_B₃
declarations.statement:
lemma cube_proj_proj_B₃ (T : MSSMACC.LinSols) :
    cubeTriLin (proj T).val (proj T).val B₃.val =
    (dot Y₃.val B₃.val)^2 * cubeTriLin T.val T.val B₃.val

declarations.name: MSSMACC.cube_proj_proj_self
declarations.statement:
lemma cube_proj_proj_self (T : MSSMACC.Sols) :
    cubeTriLin (proj T.1.1).val (proj T.1.1).val T.val =
    2 * dot Y₃.val B₃.val *
    ((dot B₃.val T.val - dot Y₃.val T.val) * cubeTriLin T.val T.val Y₃.val +
    (dot Y₃.val T.val - 2 * dot B₃.val T.val) * cubeTriLin T.val T.val B₃.val)

declarations.name: MSSMACC.cube_proj
declarations.statement:
lemma cube_proj (T : MSSMACC.Sols) :
    cubeTriLin (proj T.1.1).val (proj T.1.1).val (proj T.1.1).val =
    3 * dot Y₃.val B₃.val ^ 2 *
    ((dot B₃.val T.val - dot Y₃.val T.val) * cubeTriLin T.val T.val Y₃.val +
        (dot Y₃.val T.val - 2 * dot B₃.val T.val) * cubeTriLin T.val T.val B₃.val)

modules.title: Plane Y₃ B₃ and an orthogonal third point
modules.doc:
The plane spanned by Y₃, B₃ and third orthogonal point.

# References

* https://arxiv.org/pdf/2107.07926.pdf. [ref: Allanach:2021yjy]

declarations.name: MSSMACC.planeY₃B₃
declarations.doc:
The plane of linear solutions spanned by `Y₃`, `B₃` and `R`, a point orthogonal
to `Y₃` and `B₃`.
declarations.statement: def planeY₃B₃ (R : MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp) (a b c : ℚ) : MSSMACC.LinSols

declarations.name: MSSMACC.planeY₃B₃_val
declarations.statement:
lemma planeY₃B₃_val (R : MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp) (a b c : ℚ) :
    (planeY₃B₃ R a b c).val = a • Y₃.val + b • B₃.val + c • R.val

declarations.name: MSSMACC.planeY₃B₃_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma planeY₃B₃_smul (R : MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp) (a b c d : ℚ) :
    planeY₃B₃ R (d * a) (d * b) (d * c) = d • planeY₃B₃ R a b c

declarations.name: MSSMACC.planeY₃B₃_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma planeY₃B₃_eq (R : MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp) (a b c : ℚ) (h : a = a' ∧ b = b' ∧ c = c') :
    (planeY₃B₃ R a b c) = (planeY₃B₃ R a' b' c')

declarations.name: MSSMACC.planeY₃B₃_val_eq'
declarations.statement:
lemma planeY₃B₃_val_eq' (R : MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp) (a b c : ℚ) (hR' : R.val ≠ 0)
    (h : (planeY₃B₃ R a b c).val = (planeY₃B₃ R a' b' c').val) :
    a = a' ∧ b = b' ∧ c = c'

declarations.name: MSSMACC.planeY₃B₃_quad
declarations.statement:
lemma planeY₃B₃_quad (R : MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp) (a b c : ℚ) :
    accQuad (planeY₃B₃ R a b c).val = c * (2 * a * quadBiLin Y₃.val R.val
    + 2 * b * quadBiLin B₃.val R.val + c * quadBiLin R.val R.val)

declarations.name: MSSMACC.planeY₃B₃_cubic
declarations.statement:
lemma planeY₃B₃_cubic (R : MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp) (a b c : ℚ) :
    accCube (planeY₃B₃ R a b c).val = c ^ 2 *
    (3 * a * cubeTriLin R.val R.val Y₃.val
    + 3 * b * cubeTriLin R.val R.val B₃.val + c * cubeTriLin R.val R.val R.val)

declarations.name: MSSMACC.lineQuadAFL
declarations.doc:
The line in the plane spanned by `Y₃`, `B₃` and `R` which is in the quadratic,
as `LinSols`.
declarations.statement: def lineQuadAFL (R : MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp) (c1 c2 c3 : ℚ) : MSSMACC.LinSols

declarations.name: MSSMACC.lineQuadAFL_quad
declarations.statement:
lemma lineQuadAFL_quad (R : MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp) (c1 c2 c3 : ℚ) :
    accQuad (lineQuadAFL R c1 c2 c3).val = 0

declarations.name: MSSMACC.lineQuad
declarations.doc: The line in the plane spanned by `Y₃`, `B₃` and `R` which is in the quadratic.
declarations.statement: def lineQuad (R : MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp) (c1 c2 c3 : ℚ) : MSSMACC.QuadSols

declarations.name: MSSMACC.lineQuad_val
declarations.statement:
lemma lineQuad_val (R : MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp) (c1 c2 c3 : ℚ) :
    (lineQuad R c1 c2 c3).val = (planeY₃B₃ R
    (c2 * quadBiLin R.val R.val - 2 * c3 * quadBiLin B₃.val R.val)
    (2 * c3 * quadBiLin Y₃.val R.val - c1 * quadBiLin R.val R.val)
    (2 * c1 * quadBiLin B₃.val R.val - 2 * c2 * quadBiLin Y₃.val R.val)).val

declarations.name: MSSMACC.lineQuad_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma lineQuad_smul (R : MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp) (a b c d : ℚ) :
    lineQuad R (d * a) (d * b) (d * c) = d • lineQuad R a b c

declarations.name: MSSMACC.α₁
declarations.doc: A helper function to simplify following expressions.
declarations.statement: def α₁ (T : MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp) : ℚ

declarations.name: MSSMACC.α₂
declarations.doc: A helper function to simplify following expressions.
declarations.statement: def α₂ (T : MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp) : ℚ

declarations.name: MSSMACC.α₃
declarations.doc: A helper function to simplify following expressions.
declarations.statement: def α₃ (T : MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp) : ℚ

declarations.name: MSSMACC.lineQuad_cube
declarations.statement:
lemma lineQuad_cube (R : MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp) (c₁ c₂ c₃ : ℚ) :
    accCube (lineQuad R c₁ c₂ c₃).val =
    - 4 * (c₁ * quadBiLin B₃.val R.val - c₂ * quadBiLin Y₃.val R.val) ^ 2 *
    (α₁ R * c₁ + α₂ R * c₂ + α₃ R * c₃)

declarations.name: MSSMACC.lineCube
declarations.doc: The line in the plane spanned by `Y₃`, `B₃` and `R` which is in the cubic.
declarations.statement:
def lineCube (R : MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp) (a₁ a₂ a₃ : ℚ) :
    MSSMACC.LinSols

declarations.name: MSSMACC.lineCube_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma lineCube_smul (R : MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp) (a b c d : ℚ) :
    lineCube R (d * a) (d * b) (d * c) = d • lineCube R a b c

declarations.name: MSSMACC.lineCube_cube
declarations.statement:
lemma lineCube_cube (R : MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp) (a₁ a₂ a₃ : ℚ) :
    accCube (lineCube R a₁ a₂ a₃).val = 0

declarations.name: MSSMACC.lineCube_quad
declarations.statement:
lemma lineCube_quad (R : MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp) (a₁ a₂ a₃ : ℚ) :
    accQuad (lineCube R a₁ a₂ a₃).val =
    3 * (a₁ * cubeTriLin R.val R.val B₃.val - a₂ * cubeTriLin R.val R.val Y₃.val) *
    (α₁ R * a₁ + α₂ R * a₂ + α₃ R * a₃)

declarations.name: MSSMACC.α₃_proj
declarations.statement:
lemma α₃_proj (T : MSSMACC.Sols) : α₃ (proj T.1.1) =
    6 * dot Y₃.val B₃.val ^ 3 *
    (cubeTriLin T.val T.val Y₃.val * quadBiLin B₃.val T.val -
    cubeTriLin T.val T.val B₃.val * quadBiLin Y₃.val T.val)

declarations.name: MSSMACC.α₂_proj
declarations.statement:
lemma α₂_proj (T : MSSMACC.Sols) : α₂ (proj T.1.1) =
    - α₃ (proj T.1.1) * (dot Y₃.val T.val - 2 * dot B₃.val T.val)

declarations.name: MSSMACC.α₁_proj
declarations.statement:
lemma α₁_proj (T : MSSMACC.Sols) : α₁ (proj T.1.1) =
    - α₃ (proj T.1.1) * (dot B₃.val T.val - dot Y₃.val T.val)

declarations.name: MSSMACC.α₁_proj_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma α₁_proj_zero (T : MSSMACC.Sols) (h1 : α₃ (proj T.1.1) = 0) :
    α₁ (proj T.1.1) = 0

declarations.name: MSSMACC.α₂_proj_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma α₂_proj_zero (T : MSSMACC.Sols) (h1 : α₃ (proj T.1.1) = 0) :
    α₂ (proj T.1.1) = 0

modules.title: From charges perpendicular to `Y₃` and `B₃` to solutions
modules.doc:
The main aim of this file is to take charge assignments perpendicular to `Y₃` and `B₃` and
produce solutions to the anomaly cancellation conditions. In this regard we will define
a surjective map `toSol` from `MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp × ℚ × ℚ × ℚ` to `MSSMACC.Sols`.

To define `toSols` we define a series of other maps from various subtypes of
`MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp × ℚ × ℚ × ℚ` to `MSSMACC.Sols`. And show that these maps form a
surjection on certain subtypes of `MSSMACC.Sols`.

# References

* The main reference for the material in this file is https://arxiv.org/pdf/2107.07926.pdf.
  [ref: Allanach:2021yjy]

declarations.name: MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp.LineEqProp
declarations.doc:
A condition for the quad line in the plane spanned by R, Y₃ and B₃ to sit in the cubic,
and for the cube line to sit in the quad.
declarations.statement: def LineEqProp (R : MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp) : Prop

declarations.doc: The proposition `LineEqProp` is decidable.
declarations.statement: instance (R : MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp) : Decidable (LineEqProp R)

declarations.name: MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp.LineEqPropSol
declarations.doc:
A condition on `Sols` which we will show in `linEqPropSol_iff_proj_linEqProp` that is equivalent
to the condition that the `proj` of the solution satisfies `lineEqProp`.
declarations.statement: def LineEqPropSol (R : MSSMACC.Sols) : Prop

declarations.name: MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp.lineEqCoeff
declarations.doc:
A rational which appears in `toSolNS` acting on sols, and which being zero is
equivalent to satisfying `lineEqPropSol`.
declarations.statement: def lineEqCoeff (T : MSSMACC.Sols) : ℚ

declarations.name: MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp.lineEqPropSol_iff_lineEqCoeff_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma lineEqPropSol_iff_lineEqCoeff_zero (T : MSSMACC.Sols) :
    LineEqPropSol T ↔ lineEqCoeff T = 0

declarations.name: MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp.linEqPropSol_iff_proj_linEqProp
declarations.statement:
lemma linEqPropSol_iff_proj_linEqProp (R : MSSMACC.Sols) :
    LineEqPropSol R ↔ LineEqProp (proj R.1.1)

declarations.name: MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp.InQuadProp
declarations.doc:
A condition which is satisfied if the plane spanned by `R`, `Y₃` and `B₃` lies
entirely in the quadratic surface.
declarations.statement: def InQuadProp (R : MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp) : Prop

declarations.doc: The proposition `InQuadProp` is decidable.
declarations.statement: instance (R : MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp) : Decidable (InQuadProp R)

declarations.name: MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp.InQuadSolProp
declarations.doc:
A condition which is satisfied if the plane spanned by the solutions `R`, `Y₃` and `B₃`
lies entirely in the quadratic surface.
declarations.statement: def InQuadSolProp (R : MSSMACC.Sols) : Prop

declarations.name: MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp.quadCoeff
declarations.doc:
A rational which has two properties. It is zero for a solution `T` if and only if
that solution satisfies `inQuadSolProp`. It appears in the definition of `inQuadProj`.
declarations.statement: def quadCoeff (T : MSSMACC.Sols) : ℚ

declarations.name: MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp.inQuadSolProp_iff_quadCoeff_zero
declarations.statement: lemma inQuadSolProp_iff_quadCoeff_zero (T : MSSMACC.Sols) : InQuadSolProp T ↔ quadCoeff T = 0

declarations.name: MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp.inQuadSolProp_iff_proj_inQuadProp
declarations.doc:
The conditions `inQuadSolProp R` and `inQuadProp (proj R.1.1)` are equivalent. This is to be
expected since both `R` and `proj R.1.1` define the same plane with `Y₃` and `B₃`.
declarations.statement:
lemma inQuadSolProp_iff_proj_inQuadProp (R : MSSMACC.Sols) :
    InQuadSolProp R ↔ InQuadProp (proj R.1.1)

declarations.name: MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp.InCubeProp
declarations.doc:
A condition which is satisfied if the plane spanned by `R`, `Y₃` and `B₃` lies
entirely in the cubic surface.
declarations.statement: def InCubeProp (R : MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp) : Prop

declarations.doc: The proposition `InCubeProp` is decidable.
declarations.statement: instance (R : MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp) : Decidable (InCubeProp R)

declarations.name: MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp.InCubeSolProp
declarations.doc:
A condition which is satisfied if the plane spanned by the solutions `R`, `Y₃` and `B₃`
lies entirely in the cubic surface.
declarations.statement: def InCubeSolProp (R : MSSMACC.Sols) : Prop

declarations.name: MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp.cubicCoeff
declarations.doc:
A rational which has two properties. It is zero for a solution `T` if and only if
that solution satisfies `inCubeSolProp`. It appears in the definition of `inLineEqProj`.
declarations.statement: def cubicCoeff (T : MSSMACC.Sols) : ℚ

declarations.name: MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp.inCubeSolProp_iff_cubicCoeff_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma inCubeSolProp_iff_cubicCoeff_zero (T : MSSMACC.Sols) :
    InCubeSolProp T ↔ cubicCoeff T = 0

declarations.name: MSSMACC.AnomalyFreePerp.inCubeSolProp_iff_proj_inCubeProp
declarations.statement:

modules.title: Permutations of MSSM charges and solutions
modules.doc:
The three family MSSM charges has a family permutation of S₃⁶. This file defines this group
and its action on the MSSM.

declarations.name: MSSM.PermGroup
declarations.doc: The group of family permutations is `S₃⁶`
declarations.statement: def PermGroup

declarations.doc: The type `PermGroup` has a group instances derived from the group instance of it's target.
declarations.statement: instance : Group PermGroup

declarations.name: MSSM.chargeMap
declarations.doc: The image of an element of `permGroup` under the representation on charges.
declarations.statement: def chargeMap (f : PermGroup) : MSSMCharges.Charges →ₗ[ℚ] MSSMCharges.Charges

declarations.name: MSSM.chargeMap_toSpecies
declarations.statement:
lemma chargeMap_toSpecies (f : PermGroup) (S : MSSMCharges.Charges) (j : Fin 6) :
    toSMSpecies j (chargeMap f S) = toSMSpecies j S ∘ f j

declarations.name: MSSM.repCharges
declarations.doc: The representation of `permGroup` acting on the vector space of charges.
declarations.statement: def repCharges : Representation ℚ PermGroup (MSSMCharges).Charges

declarations.name: MSSM.repCharges_toSMSpecies
declarations.statement:
lemma repCharges_toSMSpecies (f : PermGroup) (S : MSSMCharges.Charges) (j : Fin 6) :
    toSMSpecies j (repCharges f S) = toSMSpecies j S ∘ f⁻¹ j

declarations.name: MSSM.toSpecies_sum_invariant
declarations.statement:
lemma toSpecies_sum_invariant (m : ℕ) (f : PermGroup) (S : MSSMCharges.Charges) (j : Fin 6) :
    ∑ i, ((fun a => a ^ m) ∘ toSMSpecies j (repCharges f S)) i =
    ∑ i, ((fun a => a ^ m) ∘ toSMSpecies j S) i

modules.title: SUSY N=1 chiral sector: index, configuration, and conjugation data
modules.doc:
The index data, field configuration and conjugation of the N=1 chiral sector, as a tensor species.

## i. Overview

The chiral scalars are indexed by a finite type `ι`, and a configuration is a point of `ι → ℂ`
(`ChiralScalarConfiguration`). The anti-chiral scalars are the complex conjugates of this
configuration, not independent field data. A tensor index carries one of four colours
(`ChiralColor`): holomorphic or anti-holomorphic, crossed with up or down. The four colours have
four carriers: `chiralUp` the vectors `ι → ℂ`, `chiralDown` their dual, and `antiUp` and
`antiDown` the conjugate modules of these two (`ConjModule`, in which `i` acts as `−i`).

The dual colour `τ` flips variance and keeps holomorphy, and two indices contract only when their
colours are `τ`-related, so `g^{IJ̄} D_I W D̄_J̄ W̄` type-checks. The conjugate colour `bar` flips
holomorphy and keeps variance. Contraction is the δ pairing of coordinate vectors: the basis at
`τ c` is the dual basis of the basis at `c` (`chiralTensor.instHasContrDualBases`), so a
contraction is a sum over `ι`. Every colour carries the trivial representation of `Unit`.

`chiralTensor` packages this data as a `ConjTensorSpecies`. It gives the chiral sector the generic
tensor API, and the conjugation map `conjT` in which reality and Hermiticity are stated.

## ii. Key results

- `SUSY.N1.ChiralScalarConfiguration` : the configuration space `ι → ℂ`.
- `SUSY.N1.ChiralColor` : the four colours, with the dual involution `ChiralColor.tau`.
- `SUSY.N1.chiralTensor` : the chiral sector as a `ConjTensorSpecies`.
- `SUSY.N1.chiralTensor.instHasContrDualBases` : the chiral species has dual bases at dual
    colours, matched by the identity on `ι`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The chiral scalar configuration
- B. The chiral colours and the dual involution
- C. Carrier, representation, and basis
- D. The δ structure on based finite modules
- E. The chiral-index tensor species
- F. Conjugation

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The chiral scalar configuration
## B. The chiral colours and the dual involution

## C. Carrier, representation, and basis

`chiralUp` and `chiralDown` carry `ι → ℂ` and its dual; `antiUp` and `antiDown` carry their
conjugate modules. The representation is trivial over `Unit`, and every basis is indexed by `ι`.

## D. The δ structure on based finite modules

The contraction and unit of the species are the δ structure in basis coordinates. A contraction
pairs two based modules `(M, b)` and `(N, b')` sharing the index `ι`:
`(x, y) ↦ ∑_I (b x)_I (b' y)_I` (`deltaContr₂`), with cap `∑_I b_I ⊗ b'_I` (`deltaCap₂`). The
species has no `WithMetric` instance: the metric of the chiral sector is the Kähler metric
`g_{IJ̄}`, built downstream.
## E. The chiral-index tensor species

## F. Conjugation

Conjugation is part of `chiralTensor` (§E), and the framework supplies the map `conjT` and its
laws (`conjT_conjT`, `conjT_contrT`, `conjT_eq_permT_iff`). This section normalizes `conjT` for
the two shapes the sector conjugates, the scalar `W` and the holomorphic covector `D_I W`, and
checks on components that it is complex conjugation.

The following normalize the output of `(chiralTensor (ι := ι)).conjT` back to the
canonical colour lists for scalar and anti-holomorphic covector tensors respectively.

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.ChiralScalarConfiguration
declarations.doc:
The chiral scalar configuration: a complex value for each chiral label, the sector's only field
data. An `abbrev`, so Mathlib's function-space lemmas apply to it directly.
declarations.statement: abbrev ChiralScalarConfiguration (ChiralIndexingType : Type*)

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.ChiralColor
declarations.doc:
The four colours of a chiral-sector index: holomorphy (`chiral` or `anti`) crossed with
variance (`up` or `down`).
declarations.statement: inductive ChiralColor | chiralUp | chiralDown | antiUp | antiDown

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.ChiralColor.tau
declarations.doc:
The dual colour: flips variance and keeps holomorphy. Two indices contract exactly when their
colours are `τ`-related.
declarations.statement: def tau : ChiralColor → ChiralColor

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.ChiralColor.bar
declarations.doc:
The conjugate colour: flips holomorphy and keeps variance. It commutes with `tau`
(`bar_tau`).
declarations.statement: def bar : ChiralColor → ChiralColor

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.ChiralColor.bar_bar
declarations.statement: lemma bar_bar (c : ChiralColor) : bar (bar c) = c

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.ChiralColor.bar_tau
declarations.statement: lemma bar_tau (c : ChiralColor) : bar (tau c) = tau (bar c)

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.chiralModule
declarations.doc:
The carrier of each colour: `ι → ℂ` and its dual on the holomorphic side, and their conjugate
modules (`ConjModule`, where `i` acts as `−i`) on the anti-holomorphic side.
declarations.statement: abbrev chiralModule : ChiralColor → Type

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.instAddCommGroupChiralModule
declarations.statement: instance instAddCommGroupChiralModule : ∀ c, AddCommGroup (chiralModule (ι := ι) c)

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.instModuleChiralModule
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance instModuleChiralModule : ∀ c, Module ℂ (chiralModule (ι := ι) c)

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.chiralRep
declarations.doc: The representation of each colour: trivial, over the trivial group `Unit`.
declarations.statement: def chiralRep : (c : ChiralColor) → Representation ℂ Unit (chiralModule (ι := ι) c)

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.piBasis
declarations.doc: The standard basis of `ι → ℂ`.
declarations.statement: def piBasis : Basis ι ℂ (ι → ℂ)

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.chiralBasis
declarations.doc:
The basis of each colour's carrier, indexed by `ι`: `piBasis`, its dual basis, and the
conjugate of each.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def chiralBasis : (c : ChiralColor) → Basis ι ℂ (chiralModule (ι := ι) c)

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.deltaBil₂
declarations.doc:
The δ pairing `(x, y) ↦ ∑_I (b x)_I (b' y)_I` of two based modules sharing the index `ι`,
built from Mathlib's `Basis.toDual`.
declarations.statement: def deltaBil₂ (b : Basis ι ℂ M) (b' : Basis ι ℂ N) : M →ₗ[ℂ] N →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.deltaBil₂_apply
declarations.doc: `deltaBil₂ b b' x y = ∑_I (b x)_I (b' y)_I`.
declarations.statement:
lemma deltaBil₂_apply (b : Basis ι ℂ M) (b' : Basis ι ℂ N) (x : M) (y : N) :
    deltaBil₂ b b' x y = ∑ I, b.equivFun x I * b'.equivFun y I

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.deltaContr₂
declarations.doc: The two-module δ contraction `M ⊗ N → ℂ`.
declarations.statement: def deltaContr₂ (b : Basis ι ℂ M) (b' : Basis ι ℂ N) : M ⊗[ℂ] N →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.deltaContr₂_tmul
declarations.doc: `deltaContr₂ b b' (x ⊗ₜ y) = ∑_I (b x)_I (b' y)_I`.
declarations.statement:
lemma deltaContr₂_tmul (b : Basis ι ℂ M) (b' : Basis ι ℂ N) (x : M) (y : N) :
    deltaContr₂ b b' (x ⊗ₜ[ℂ] y) = ∑ I, b.equivFun x I * b'.equivFun y I

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.deltaContr₂_tmul_basis
declarations.doc: `deltaContr₂ b b' (x ⊗ₜ b' J) = x_J`: pairing with the second basis reads off a coordinate.
declarations.statement:
lemma deltaContr₂_tmul_basis (b : Basis ι ℂ M) (b' : Basis ι ℂ N) (x : M) (J : ι) :
    deltaContr₂ b b' (x ⊗ₜ[ℂ] b' J) = b.equivFun x J

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.deltaContr₂_basis_basis
declarations.doc: `deltaContr₂ b b' (b I ⊗ₜ b' J) = δ_{IJ}`: the two bases are δ-dual.
declarations.statement:
lemma deltaContr₂_basis_basis (b : Basis ι ℂ M) (b' : Basis ι ℂ N) (I J : ι) :
    deltaContr₂ b b' (b I ⊗ₜ[ℂ] b' J) = if I = J then 1 else 0

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.deltaContr₂_comm
declarations.doc: `deltaContr₂ b b' (x ⊗ₜ y) = deltaContr₂ b' b (y ⊗ₜ x)`: swapping slots swaps the two bases.
declarations.statement:
lemma deltaContr₂_comm (b : Basis ι ℂ M) (b' : Basis ι ℂ N) (x : M) (y : N) :
    deltaContr₂ b b' (x ⊗ₜ[ℂ] y) = deltaContr₂ b' b (y ⊗ₜ[ℂ] x)

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.deltaCap₂
declarations.doc: The two-module δ cap `∑_I b_I ⊗ b'_I ∈ M ⊗ N`.
declarations.statement: def deltaCap₂ (b : Basis ι ℂ M) (b' : Basis ι ℂ N) : M ⊗[ℂ] N

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.deltaCap₂_comm
declarations.doc: `comm (deltaCap₂ b b') = deltaCap₂ b' b`: swapping the two factors swaps the two bases.
declarations.statement:
lemma deltaCap₂_comm (b : Basis ι ℂ M) (b' : Basis ι ℂ N) :
    TensorProduct.comm ℂ M N (deltaCap₂ b b') = deltaCap₂ b' b

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.deltaUnit₂_symm
declarations.doc:
The `unit_symm` law (two-module, `toSpanSingleton` form): `deltaCap₂ b' b` is the swap of
`deltaCap₂ b b'`.
declarations.statement:
lemma deltaUnit₂_symm (b : Basis ι ℂ M) (b' : Basis ι ℂ N) :
    LinearMap.toSpanSingleton ℂ _ (deltaCap₂ b' b) 1 =
      LinearMap.lTensor N (LinearEquiv.refl ℂ M).toLinearMap
        (TensorProduct.comm ℂ M N (LinearMap.toSpanSingleton ℂ _ (deltaCap₂ b b') 1))

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.deltaContr₂_unit
declarations.doc:
The snake identity (two-module, `contr_unit` law): contracting `x ∈ M` into the `M`-leg of
`deltaCap₂ b' b ∈ N ⊗ M` returns `x`.
declarations.statement:
lemma deltaContr₂_unit (b : Basis ι ℂ M) (b' : Basis ι ℂ N) (x : M) :
    (TensorProduct.lid ℂ M) ((deltaContr₂ b b').rTensor M
      ((TensorProduct.assoc ℂ M N M).symm
        (x ⊗ₜ[ℂ] LinearMap.toSpanSingleton ℂ _ (deltaCap₂ b' b) 1))) = x

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.chiralTensor
declarations.doc:
The chiral-index tensor species with its conjugation. Its contraction is the δ pairing of a
colour with its dual `τ c`, its unit the δ cap, and its conjugation flips holomorphy by
`ChiralColor.bar`.
declarations.statement:
def chiralTensor : ConjTensorSpecies ℂ ChiralColor Unit (chiralModule (ι := ι)) (fun _ => ι)
    (chiralRep (ι := ι)) (chiralBasis (ι := ι))

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.chiralTensor_contr_chiralBasis
declarations.doc: The chiral contraction of two basis vectors is the Kronecker δ.
declarations.statement:
lemma chiralTensor_contr_chiralBasis (d : ChiralColor) (x₁ x₂ : ι) :
    (chiralTensor (ι := ι)).contr d
        (chiralBasis (ι := ι) d x₁ ⊗ₜ[ℂ] chiralBasis (ι := ι) ((chiralTensor (ι := ι)).τ d) x₂)
      = if x₁ = x₂ then 1 else 0

    (chiralTensor (ι := ι)).Tensor ![]

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.conjChiralCovector
declarations.doc:
Conjugation of a holomorphic covector, normalized to the anti-holomorphic covector colour
list `![antiDown]`.
declarations.statement:
def conjChiralCovector
    (t : (chiralTensor (ι := ι)).Tensor ![chiralDown]) :
    (chiralTensor (ι := ι)).Tensor ![antiDown]

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.toScalar_conjScalar
declarations.doc:
For scalar tensors, `toScalar` of the normalized tensor conjugate is the complex conjugate of
`toScalar`.
declarations.statement:
lemma toScalar_conjScalar (t : (chiralTensor (ι := ι)).Tensor ![]) :
    (conjScalar t).toScalar = star t.toScalar

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.repr_conjChiralCovector
declarations.doc:
Component formula for the holomorphic covector conjugate: the `![I]` basis component of
`conjChiralCovector t` is the complex conjugate of the `![I]` component of `t`.
declarations.statement:
lemma repr_conjChiralCovector
    (t : (chiralTensor (ι := ι)).Tensor ![chiralDown]) (I : ι) :
    (basis (S := (chiralTensor (ι := ι)).toTensorSpecies) ![antiDown]).repr
        (conjChiralCovector t) ![I] =
      star ((basis (S := (chiralTensor (ι := ι)).toTensorSpecies) ![chiralDown]).repr t ![I])

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.conjChiralCovector_add
declarations.doc: Conjugation of a holomorphic covector is additive.
declarations.statement:
lemma conjChiralCovector_add
    (t₁ t₂ : (chiralTensor (ι := ι)).Tensor ![chiralDown]) :
    conjChiralCovector (t₁ + t₂) = conjChiralCovector t₁ + conjChiralCovector t₂

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.conjChiralCovector_smul
declarations.doc:
Conjugation of a holomorphic covector is conjugate-linear: a scalar `r` pulls out as
`star r`.
declarations.statement:
lemma conjChiralCovector_smul (r : ℂ)
    (t : (chiralTensor (ι := ι)).Tensor ![chiralDown]) :
    conjChiralCovector (r • t) = star r • conjChiralCovector t

modules.title: SUSY N=1 superpotential
modules.doc:
The superpotential of the N=1 chiral sector, and its gradient as a chiral tensor.

## i. Overview

A superpotential on a domain `D` of configurations is a function `W` that is holomorphic on `D`.
It coerces to that function, so `W u` is its value at `u`.
Its gradient `∂_I W` is the covector of colour `chiralDown` whose components are the holomorphic
Wirtinger derivatives of `W`. The conjugates `W̄` and `∂̄_J̄ W̄` are `star W` and
`conjChiralCovector` of the gradient.

## ii. Key results

- `SUSY.N1.Superpotential` : a superpotential, holomorphic on a domain.
- `SUSY.N1.Superpotential.dW` : its gradient, a `chiralDown` covector.
- `SUSY.N1.Superpotential.repr_dW` : the components of the gradient are `∂_I W`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The superpotential
- B. The gradient

## iv. References

* None.

## B. The gradient

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.Superpotential
declarations.doc:
A superpotential on the domain `D`: a function `W` of the chiral configuration, holomorphic on
`D`.
declarations.statement:
structure Superpotential (ι : Type) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (D : Set (ChiralScalarConfiguration ι)) where
  /-- The superpotential `W`. -/
  W : ChiralScalarConfiguration ι → ℂ
  /-- `W` is holomorphic on `D`. -/
  holomorphic : ∀ u ∈ D, DifferentiableAt ℂ W u

declarations.doc: A superpotential is applied as the function `W`.
declarations.statement: instance : CoeFun (Superpotential ι D) (fun _ => ChiralScalarConfiguration ι → ℂ)

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.Superpotential.dW
declarations.doc: The gradient `∂_I W` of the superpotential, a covector of colour `chiralDown`.
declarations.statement:
def dW (W : Superpotential ι D) (u : ChiralScalarConfiguration ι) :
    (chiralTensor (ι := ι)).Tensor ![chiralDown]

declarations.name: SUSY.N1.Superpotential.repr_dW
declarations.doc: The `I`-th component of the gradient is `∂_I W`.
declarations.statement:
lemma repr_dW (W : Superpotential ι D) (u : ChiralScalarConfiguration ι) (I : ι) :
    (basis (S := (chiralTensor (ι := ι)).toTensorSpecies) ![chiralDown]).repr (W.dW u) ![I] =
      dWirtingerCoord W I u

modules.title: Charges allowing terms
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

To each charge spectrum `x : ChargeSpectrum 𝓩` we say it
allows the potential term `T : PotentialTerm`, if one of the charges associated with that
potential term is zero.

What this means, is that there is a choice of charges from the charge spectrum `x` that
can be assigned to the fields in the potential term `T` such that the total charge is zero,
and therefore that the term is present in the potential. The presence of
absence of certain terms is of phenomenological importance.

This concept is captured by the proposition `AllowsTerm`.

In addition to this, for each potential term `T`, we define a function `allowsTermForm`
which takes three elements of `𝓩`, `a`, `b`, and `c` and returns a charge spectrum
which allows the term `T`. We will show in `allowsTerm_iff_subset_allowsTermForm`
that any charge spectrum that allows a term `T` has a subset which can be expressed as
`allowsTermForm a b c T` for some `a`, `b`, and `c`.

We also define the propositions `AllowsTermQ5 x q5 T` and `AllowsTermQ10 x q10 T`
which correspond to the condition that adding a charge `q5` to the `Q5` charges of
the charge spectrum `x`, or adding a charge `q10` to the `Q10` charges of the
charge spectrum `x`, leads to a zero charge in the charges of potential term `T`.

## ii. Key results

- `AllowsTerm` : The proposition that a charge spectrum allows a potential term.
- `allowsTermForm` : A function which for each potential term `T` and three charges
  `a`, `b`, and `c` returns a charge spectrum which allows the term `T`,
  and such that any charge spectrum allowing `T` has a subset of this form.
- `AllowsTermQ5` : The proposition that adding a charge `q5` to the `Q5` charges
  of a charge spectrum `x` allows the potential term `T` due to the addition of that charge.
- `AllowsTermQ10` : The proposition that adding a charge `q10` to the `Q10` charges
  of a charge spectrum `x` allows the potential term `T` due to the addition of that charge.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Charge spectrums allowing potential terms
  - A.1. Decidability of `AllowsTerm`
  - A.2. Monotonicity of `AllowsTerm`
- B. Forms of charges which allow potential terms
  - B.1. `allowsTermForm` allows the potential term
  - B.2. Subset relations for `allowsTermForm`
  - B.3. Card of `allowsTermForm`
  - B.4. If `AllowsTerm` then subset equal to `allowsTermForm a b c T`
  - B.5. `AllowsTerm` if and only if subset equal to `allowsTermForm a b c T`
  - B.6. Cardinality of subset allowing potential term
- C. Allowing a potential term by insertion of a `Q5` charge
  - C.1. Decidability of `AllowsTermQ5`
  - C.2. AllowsTermQ5 or AllowsTerm from AllowsTerm with inserted of `Q5` charge
  - C.3. AllowsTerm with inserted of `Q5` charge from AllowsTermQ5
  - C.4. AllowsTerm with inserted of `Q5` charge iff AllowsTermQ5 or AllowsTerm
- D. Allowing a potential term by insertion of a `Q10` charge
  - D.1. Decidability of `AllowsTermQ5`
  - D.2. AllowsTermQ10 or AllowsTerm from AllowsTerm with inserted of `Q10` charge
  - D.3. AllowsTerm with inserted of `Q10` charge from AllowsTermQ5
  - D.4. AllowsTerm with inserted of `Q10` charge iff AllowsTermQ10 or AllowsTerm

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. Charge spectrums allowing potential terms

We first define the proposition `AllowsTerm`, which for a charge spectrum `x : ChargeSpectrum 𝓩`
and a potential term `T : PotentialTerm`, is true if the zero charge is in the set of
charges associated with that potential term.

That is, if there is some choice of representations present in the theory which will allow that
potential term via symmetry.

### A.1. Decidability of `AllowsTerm`

We define the decidability of `AllowsTerm` through `ofPotentialTerm'` rather than
`ofPotentialTerm` due to the speed of the former compared to the latter.

### A.2. Monotonicity of `AllowsTerm`

The proposition `AllowsTerm` is monotone in its charge spectrum argument.
That is if a charge spectrum `y` is a subset of a charge spectrum `x`,
and `y` allows a potential term `T`, then `x` also allows that potential term `T`.

## B. Forms of charges which allow potential terms

We now define the function `allowsTermForm` which for each potential term `T`
and three charges `a`, `b`, and `c` returns a charge spectrum which allows the term `T`.

These charges are in a minimal form, in the sense that any charge spectrum allowing `T`
has a subset of this form.

### B.1. `allowsTermForm` allows the potential term

Any charge spectrum of the form `allowsTermForm a b c T` allows the potential term `T`.

### B.2. Subset relations for `allowsTermForm`

For any potential term `T` except for `W¹ᵢⱼₖₗ 10ⁱ 10ʲ 10ᵏ 5̄Mˡ` or `W²ᵢⱼₖ 10ⁱ 10ʲ 10ᵏ 5̄Hd`,
a charge spectrum `allowsTermForm a b c T` is a subset of another charge spectrum
`allowsTermForm a' b' c' T` if they are equal.

The reason this does not work for `W1` an `W2` is due to the presence of three
charges in the 10d representation.

### B.3. Card of `allowsTermForm`

The cardinality of the charge spectrum `allowsTermForm a b c T` is always
less than or equal to the degree of the potential term `T`.

### B.4. If `AllowsTerm` then subset equal to `allowsTermForm a b c T`

We now show one of the more important properties of `allowsTermForm`.
Namely that if a charge spectrum `x`
allows a potential term `T`, then there exists charges `a`, `b`, and `c` such that
`allowsTermForm a b c T ⊆ x`.

The proof of this result is rather long, relying on case-by-case analysis of each
of the potential terms of interest.

### B.5. `AllowsTerm` if and only if subset equal to `allowsTermForm a b c T`

We now lift the previous result to show that a charge spectrum `x`
allows a potential term `T` if and only if there exists charges `a`, `b`, and `c` such that
`allowsTermForm a b c T ⊆ x`.

Given what has already been shown, this result is now trivial.

### B.6. Cardinality of subset allowing potential term

We show that if a charge spectrum `x` allows a potential term `T`,
then there exists a subset of `x` which allows `T` and whose cardinality is less than or equal
to the degree of `T`.

This follows from the fact that `allowsTermForm a b c T` always has cardinality
less than or equal to the degree of `T`.

## C. Allowing a potential term by insertion of a `Q5` charge

We now study what happens when we add a charge `q5` to the `Q5` charges of a charge spectrum `x`.
We define the proposition `AllowsTermQ5 x q5 T` which is true if adding the charge `q5`
to the `Q5` charges of `x` allows the potential term `T` due to the addition of that charge.

We prove a number of properties of this proposition, including its relation
to `AllowsTerm` and its decidability.

### C.1. Decidability of `AllowsTermQ5`

We show that if the type `𝓩` has decidable equality, then the proposition
`AllowsTermQ5 x q5 T` is decidable for any charge spectrum `x`, charge `q5`, and
potential term `T`.

### C.2. AllowsTermQ5 or AllowsTerm from AllowsTerm with inserted of `Q5` charge

We show that if a charge spectrum `x` with an inserted charge `q5`
allows a potential term `T`, then either the charge spectrum `x`
allows that potential term `T` *due to* the addition of that charge,
or the charge spectrum `x` already allows that potential term `T`.

### C.3. AllowsTerm with inserted of `Q5` charge from AllowsTermQ5

We show that if a charge spectrum `x` allows a potential term `T`
*due to* the addition of a charge `q5`, then the charge spectrum `x` with that charge inserted
allows that potential term `T`.

### C.4. AllowsTerm with inserted of `Q5` charge iff AllowsTermQ5 or AllowsTerm

We show that the charge spectrum `x` with that charge inserted
allows that potential term `T` if and only if either the charge spectrum `x`
allows that potential term `T` *due to* the addition of that charge,
or the charge spectrum `x` already allows that potential term `T`.

## D. Allowing a potential term by insertion of a `Q10` charge

We now replicate the previous section, but for the insertion of a `Q10` charge, rather
than a `Q5` charge.

We study what happens when we add a charge `q10` to the `Q10` charges of a charge spectrum `x`.
We define the proposition `AllowsTermQ10 x q10 T` which is true if adding the charge `q10`
to the `Q10` charges of `x` allows the potential term `T` due to the addition of that charge.

We prove a number of properties of this proposition, including its relation
to `AllowsTerm` and its decidability.

### D.1. Decidability of `AllowsTermQ5`

We show that if the type `𝓩` has decidable equality, then the proposition
`AllowsTermQ10 x q10 T` is decidable for any charge spectrum `x`, charge `q10`, and
potential term `T`.

### D.2. AllowsTermQ10 or AllowsTerm from AllowsTerm with inserted of `Q10` charge

We show that if a charge spectrum `x` with an inserted charge `q10`
allows a potential term `T`, then either the charge spectrum `x`
allows that potential term `T` *due to* the addition of that charge,
or the charge spectrum `x` already allows that potential term `T`.

### D.3. AllowsTerm with inserted of `Q10` charge from AllowsTermQ5

We show that if a charge spectrum `x` allows a potential term `T`
*due to* the addition of a charge `q10`, then the charge spectrum `x` with that charge inserted
allows that potential term `T`.

### D.4. AllowsTerm with inserted of `Q10` charge iff AllowsTermQ10 or AllowsTerm

We show that the charge spectrum `x` with that charge inserted
allows that potential term `T` if and only if either the charge spectrum `x`
allows that potential term `T` *due to* the addition of that charge,
or the charge spectrum `x` already allows that potential term `T`.

modules.title: Charge Spectrum
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we define the charge spectrum of a `SU(5)` SUSY GUT theory with
additional charges (usually `U(1)`) valued in `𝓩` satisfying the condition of:
- The optional existence of a `Hd` particle in the `bar 5` representation.
- The optional existence of a `Hu` particle in the `5` representation.
- The optional existence of matter in the `bar 5` representation.
- The optional existence of matter in the `10` representation.

The charge spectrum contains the information of the *unique* charges of each type of particle
present in theory. Importantly, the charge spectrum does not contain information
about the multiplicity of those charges.

With just the charge spectrum of the theory it is possible to put a number of constraints
on the theory, most notably phenomenological constraints.

By keeping the presence of `Hd` and `Hu` optional, we can define a number of useful properties
of the charge spectrum, which can help in searching for viable theories.

## ii. Key results

- `ChargeSpectrum 𝓩` : The type of charge spectra with charges of type `𝓩`, which is usually
  `ℤ`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The definition of the charge spectrum
  - A.1. Extensionality properties
  - A.2. Relation to products
  - A.3. Rendering
- B. The subset relation
- C. The empty charge spectrum
- D. The cardinality of a charge spectrum
- E. The power set of a charge spectrum
- F. Finite sets of charge spectra with values
  - F.1. Cardinality of finite sets of charge spectra with values

## iv. References

* None — these charge spectra were created specifically for the purpose of
  Physlib; there is no external reference.

sections.text: ## A. The definition of the charge spectrum

### A.1. Extensionality properties

We prove extensionality properties for `ChargeSpectrum 𝓩`, that is
conditions of when two elements of `ChargeSpectrum 𝓩` are equal.
We also show that when `𝓩` has decidable equality, so does `ChargeSpectrum 𝓩`.

### A.2. Relation to products

We show that `ChargeSpectrum 𝓩` is equivalent to the product
`Option 𝓩 × Option 𝓩 × Finset 𝓩 × Fin 𝓩`.

In an old implementation this was definitionally true, it is not so now.
### A.3. Rendering

## B. The subset relation

We define a `HasSubset` and `HasSSubset` instance on `ChargeSpectrum 𝓩`.
## C. The empty charge spectrum
## D. The cardinality of a charge spectrum
